questionable

Aubrey connected on 52-yard field goals in both the first and third quarters, although his PAT in the second missed wide left. It was the second missed extra-point try of the season for Aubrey and his seventh miss overall, although five of those failed kicks have come on field-goal attempts from 50-plus yards. The Cowboys will stay home for Week 11 against the Titans, who give up 26.6 points per game (27th in the NFL) and have yielded 40-plus points in each of their last two contests.

Abanikanda made his 2026 regular-season debut against the 49ers in Week 10, when he operated as the Cowboys' RB2 behind Javonte Williams. Abanikanda finished that contest with two carries for eight yards and a two-yard catch on his lone target in what ended as a 46-40 loss for Dallas. With both Tyler Goodson (knee) and Malik Davis (hip) on injured reserve, Abanikanda figures to be elevated to the Cowboys' active roster for Week 11 against the Titans on Sunday.

Bland will likely miss time after suffering a high-ankle sprain in Week 10 against the 49ers. It's unclear how much time he'll be sidelined, but the injury could be related to an issue that plagued Bland during the practice week. Cobie Durant will likely fill in for Bland should the standout cornerback miss any time.

Booker is expected to miss multiple weeks after injuring his ankle in the first half of Sunday's game against the 49ers, per Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com. The 22-year-old may be able to avoid being placed on injured reserve with the Cowboys' bye coming in Week 14. T.J. Bass will likely slot into Booker's right guard spot.

Williams had a near monopoly on the Cowboys' running back touches, but he worked hard for everything he got against a talented 49ers front seven. The veteran back averaged under 4.0 yards per carry for the seventh time this season, but he did eclipse 60 rushing yards for the third time in the last four games. Williams will take 692 rushing yards and nine rush TDs -- along with a 25-131-1 receiving line -- into a Week 11 home matchup against the Titans next Sunday.

Despite his own impressive numbers, Lamb played second fiddle to George Pickens for a change, as the latter doubled up the former in receptions and did the same with a yard to spare in receiving yards. Nevertheless, Lamb still put together a solid performance that included his eighth touchdown reception of the season, a spectacular leaping one-handed one-yard grab late in the fourth quarter. Lamb now is up to five consecutive double-digit target tallies and has at least 70 receiving yards in four of the last five contests heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the vulnerable Titans defense.

Playing catch-up from the second quarter on did wonders for Prescott's fantasy production, as the veteran quarterback sent 38 total targets in the direction of the talented trio of George Pickens, CeeDee Lamb and Ryan Flournoy alone. Prescott connected with Pickens for three of his scoring strikes, which went for 35, 39 and five yards. Flournoy (11 yards) and Lamb (one yard) accounted for the final two in the fourth quarter, and Prescott added a two-point conversion run after the final scoring toss with an admirable diving attempt on which he made contact with the pylon with the extended ball. Prescott tied a career high with his TD pass total, while his passing yardage was a season high. He should have an opportunity to put together a successful encore next Sunday, as a Week 11 home matchup with the vulnerable Titans secondary awaits.

After watching fellow wideout CeeDee Lamb have several monster performances through the first half of the season, Pickens stepped up and took his turn in his return from a one-game absence due to a hamstring injury. Pickens was peppered with targets from Dak Prescott all afternoon, and the star receiver finished with career-high reception and target totals and a season high in receiving yards. Pickens struck from 35, 39 and five yards out on his trio of scoring grabs, which constituted Dak Prescott's first three TD passes on the day. A now clearly healthy Pickens is up to a 50-678-5 line on 80 targets for the season heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Titans next Sunday.

Dallas played catch-up for much of the second half in the offensive slugfest, so quarterback Dak Prescott took to the air 51 times. Flournoy got seven of those targets, finishing third on the team behind George Pickens (18) and CeeDee Lamb (13). Flournoy's six receptions and 71 yards were both his second-highest figures so far this season, and the TD was his third in the past five weeks. That last stat in particular gives him relevance in most fantasy leagues, especially in matchups during which Prescott is expected to air it out often. The Cowboys will seek a much-needed win next Sunday at home against Tennessee.

Ogbonnia suffered a finger injury in the second quarter and was subsequently deemed questionable to return. However, he was able to get back on the field after halftime. Ogbonnia will thus continue to play a key role along Dallas' defensive line.

The Cowboys activated Bullard from injured reserve Saturday. The defensive tackle has been sidelined since sustaining a calf injury during the Cowboys' Week 3 loss to the Ravens. Bullard is set to suit up as a rotational defensive lineman behind starter Otito Ogbonnia.

Porter upgraded to limited participation in Friday's practice after missing the first two Week 10 prep sessions and the Cowboys' Week 9 win over the Colts. The cornerback is all set to return to the field alongside DaRon Bland to anchor the Cowboys' secondary for a big matchup with one of the NFC's top contenders.

The Cowboys technically still have one elevation to use on Mitchell this season, but they instead will opt to sign him to the active roster for Week 10. His signing gives the Cowboys extra depth at tight end, as the team will be without Jake Ferguson (knee) for Sunday's game against the 49ers.

The cornerback was a limited participant Wednesday. Abrams-Draine had to miss the Broncos' win over the Panthers in Week 9 ahead of the team's Week 10 bye. Now that he's had a week off to get healthy, he appears ready to play Sunday against Las Vegas.

A full practice participant for the second day in a row, Waddle looks to be close to clearing the NFL's concussion protocol after he sustained the head injury in a Nov. 8 win over the Panthers. Assuming he can receive clearance from an independent neurologist by the weekend, Waddle will be removed from the protocol and suit up Sunday versus the Raiders.

Per Tom Pelissero of Netflix, the deal is worth $67 million and keeps Moss on the Broncos' books through 2030. A 2023 third-round draft pick, Moss has started in all 39 of his appearances over his first three-plus seasons in Denver and leads the NFL with 19 pass breakups since the start of the 2025 campaign, per Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com. With 2024 NFL Defensive Player of the Year Pat Surtain under contract through 2029, the Broncos should have one of the league's top cornerback tandems in place for the next several seasons. Moss is currently listed on the Broncos' Week 11 injury report while he recovers from a concussion sustained in a Nov. 8 win over the Panthers, but he was a full participant Wednesday and looks likely to clear the five-step protocol ahead of Sunday's game against the Raiders.

Jones was unable to play in Week 9 against the Panthers due to a hamstring injury that he picked up against the Cowboys in Week 8. He's had extra time to recover thanks to the Week 10 bye, and he'll have two more chances to increase his practice participation ahead of Sunday's game against Las Vegas.

It appears Prentice entered the league's concussion protocol following the Broncos' Week 9 win over the Panthers. He had additional time to recover courtesy of the Week 10 bye, so the veteran fullback should be available for Sunday's AFC West tilt against the Raiders.

Wednesday was Hufanga's first full practice since he hurt his ankle back in Week 5 against the Chargers. Barring any setbacks, it looks like he'll have a good chance to return to game action Sunday versus the Raiders.

Lohner opened the season on injured reserve after undergoing a procedure on his lower body in June. It appears the 25-year-old could make his return soon, as the Broncos have 21 days to officially activate him from IR before he becomes ineligible to return in 2026.

Singleton's six stops were a season low, but he still finished second on the Broncos in that category behind Jahdae Barron (eight). It's been a career year for Singleton, who is up to an NFL-leading 107 total tackles through nine regular-season games, which includes 2.0 sacks.

Trautman failed to record a catch across six games between Weeks 2 and 7, but he has logged two receptions in each of his two outings. His 41 offensive snaps ended up being ahead of fellow tight end Evan Engram (38), although the latter has been more involved in the Broncos' offensive game plan than Trautman. The Broncos' next game takes place in Week 11 against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 22.

Nineteen of Mims' 24 snaps came on offense, although he logged only two touches in the process. He hasn't seen more than four targets in a game this season, with most of his output coming on special teams as a returner on both kickoffs and punts. The Broncos are on a bye for Week 10, so their next game will take place in Week 11 against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 22

Franklin drew a 27-yard pass interference penalty on the Broncos' second offensive play of the game, but the third-year wide receiver didn't log his first catch until early in the fourth quarter. He has operated in a rotational role for most of the season, and even with Jaylen Waddle in the league's concussion protocol, Franklin will likely maintain that workload following the Broncos' Week 10 bye.

The four catches matched Engram's season high, and his 33 yards were his most since Week 5. It goes without saying, but Engram is well off the fantasy radar at tight end. He has 17 catches for 169 yards and one touchdown through nine games, averaging a career-low 18.8 yards per contest.
Lutz's field-goal tries were good from 26 and 48 yards. The 32-year-old has now converted 16 of his 19 field-goal attempts and all 16 of his extra-point tries across nine appearances this season.

Dobbins saw 13 fewer carries than rookie running back Jonah Coleman (17-57-1) in the game. The four rushes were a season low for Dobbins, and he figures to continue to operate as the team's No. 2 option in the backfield moving forward.

Bryant was activated from IR on Saturday after recovering from an ankle injury, and he came up big late in Sunday's contest, hauling in a 26-yard TD strike from Bo Nix with less than six minutes left in the fourth quarter for what proved to be the game-winning score. The second-year wideout's clutch play came after Jaylen Waddle (concussion) had left the game, and if a Week 10 bye doesn't give him enough time to recover, Bryant could see an elevated role in Week 11 against the Raiders.

The five grabs and nine targets led the Broncos on the day, but Pat Bryant just edged him out for the receiving yards lead. The highlight of Sutton's solid performance was a three-yard TD from Bo Nix in the first quarter, as none of his receptions went for longer than 12 yards. Denver gets a well-timed bye in Week 10, but if Jaylen Waddle (concussion) isn't cleared to play on the other side of it, Sutton could see bigger volume in Week 11 against the Raiders. On the season, the long-time Bronco sports a 25-266-2 line on 46 targets through nine games.

The rookie has seized control of the lead-back role for the Broncos, with his 21 touches dwarfing J.K. Dobbins' five, and Coleman's nine-yard TD run early in the fourth quarter put his team in the lead for good. Coleman has piled up 261 scrimmage yards and two rushing touchdowns over the last three games, and there's no reason to think his role will shrink on the other side of a Week 10 bye.

The Broncos had the home team right where they wanted them heading into the fourth quarter -- holding a lead -- and Nix worked his usual magic over the final 15 minutes, leading back-to-back touchdown drives capped by a nine-yard TD run from Jonah Coleman and a 26-yard strike to Pat Bryant for what proved to be the winning score. Nix did throw his first INT since Week 3 in the win, but he heads into a Week 10 bye with Denver riding a five-game win streak that has taken it to the top of the AFC West.

Tillman was on the injury report ahead of the Week 9 meeting with Carolina due to a hamstring issue. However, he will avoid his second absence of the 2026 campaign. The 28-year-old has appeared in seven games for the Broncos this season, amassing 19 total tackles (10 solo).

Uwazurike wasn't able to practice at all this week due to a shoulder issue. He started seven of Denver's first eight games, but he's now required to miss the team's next four contests. Third-round rookie Tyler Onyedim could see the first gameday action of his career as a result.

A limited participant for Wednesday's walkthrough, Vaki continued to operate with some restrictions while the Lions held a more traditional practice Thursday. Vaki's involvement in any capacity is nonetheless a good sign for his Week 11 status, though he may need to upgrade to full participation Friday to avoid carrying an injury designation into Sunday's game versus the Buccaneers.

McCreary recorded his first interception of the season in Week 10, when he jumped in front of a pass from Tommy DeVito -- who took over under center for the Patriots after Drake Maye injured his ankle in the first quarter -- that was intended for Mack Hollins, although the Lions' offense couldn't convert the takeaway into points. McCreary is up to 38 tackles (28 solo), including 1.0 sacks, 10 pass defenses and one forced fumble across nine regular-season games.

A hip injury has prevented Reed from playing in each of the Lions' last two games, and the veteran defensive back expressed pessimism Wednesday about his ability to suit up for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers, per Jeremy Reisman of PrideofDetroit.com. If Reed doesn't play in Week 11, then Khalil Dorsey (ankle) would likely start opposite Rock Ya-Sin at outside cornerback.

Joseph was a full participant in his return to the active roster Wednesday. The free safety is set to make his 2026 debut in Week 11 against the Buccaneers, finally reuniting with strong safety Brian Branch after both spent lengthy periods on the Lions' reserve lists.

Hutchinson's move to IR was merely a formality after he was diagnosed with a torn ACL in his right knee following his early exit from this past Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munich. The No. 2 overall pick in the 2022 NFL Draft has now succumbed to two season-ending injuries through his first five years in the league, after a fractured tibia and fibula in his left leg cut short his 2024 campaign.

A healthy inactive for two of the Lions' first four games of the season, Conklin has now suited up for five consecutive contests. However, the veteran tight end has been handling a limited role, logging less than one-third of the offensive snaps in any of his seven appearances on the season while compiling a 2-11-0 receiving line on three targets.

Saylors played six snaps on offense while serving as a No. 3 option behind Jahmyr Gibbs and Sione Vaki in the backfield. Saylors was on the field for 20 snaps with the special-teams unit, and he'll continue to be primarily a special-teams asset in Week 11 against the Buccaneers.

Wright tied season highs in both receiving yards and catches during Sunday's win, and his 39 snaps on offense were second-most among Lions tight ends behind Sam LaPorta (56). Wright has accumulated seven catches on eight target for 42 yards across nine regular-season games, and he's mostly served as a blocking tight end on the Lions' offense.

Mays has already missed two contests due to an ankle injury he suffered Week 8 versus Minnesota. Head coach Dan Campbell said Tuesday that Mays is probably going to be out again this Sunday against the Bucs. That means Juice Scruggs will likely make another start at center for Detroit.

The Lions didn't need to throw it much, as Drake Maye (ankle) got knocked out of the game for the Patriots early, and LaPorta simply didn't get many chances to make an impact. It was the worst performance of the season for the fourth-year tight end, but LaPorta's gone four straight games without reaching 40 receiving yards or getting into the end zone. He'll try to break out in Week 11 against the Buccaneers.

Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs monopolized the Lions' offense on the day, scoring four of the team's five TDs, and there wasn't much production left over for Williams. The fifth-year wideout has topped 50 receiving yards just three times this season, and he'll take a 32-518-5 line on 51 targets through nine games into a Week 11 battle with the Buccaneers.

The Lions didn't need to throw it much, as Drake Maye (ankle) got knocked out of the game for the Patriots early. St. Brown took full advantage of the volume he saw however, scoring on a 56-yard catch and run in the first quarter and then taking another short pass from Jared Goff and turning it into a 28-yard TD in the third. It was St. Brown's third multi-TD game of the season but his first since Week 2, and he'll take a 65-755-7 line on 91 targets through nine games into a Week 11 clash with the Buccaneers.
Bates did not attempt a field goal in the contest. He remains 16-for-17 on field-goal attempts and moves to 29-for-29 on PATs through nine regular-season games in 2026.

It was a quiet day for TeSlaa, with the Lions' offense being powered by usual suspects Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs, with the latter duo combining for four touchdowns (three receiving, one rushing). TeSlaa was the other Lions player to find the end zone, which took place early in the second quarter on a 12-yard touchdown pass from Jared Goff. It was the first touchdown catch of the season for TeSlaa, who found the end zone six times across 17 regular-season games during his rookie campaign in 2025. He has been the Lions' distant WR3 behind St. Brown and Jameson Williams, and that shouldn't change ahead of the team's Week 11 tilt against the Buccaneers on Nov. 22.

Drake Maye (ankle) got knocked out of the game early for New England, setting the stage for the rout, and Gibbs took full advantage as he set new season highs in receiving yards and scrimmage yards. It's the fourth time in 2026 that the star RB has topped 150 rushing yards, and his fourth game with multiple TDs. Gibbs has amassed 1,384 scrimmage yards and 13 total touchdowns through nine contests as he gets ready to face a stingy Buccaneers run defense in Week 11.

A potential barn burner versus Drake Maye never materialized when the New England quarterback left the game early with an ankle injury, but Goff and the Detroit offense still held up their end of the bargain. Two of Goff's TDs went to Amon-Ra St. Brown, including a 56-yard catch-and-run score in the first quarter, while Isaac TeSlaa also hauled in a 12-yard score in the second. Goff will take an 18:4 TD:INT through nine games into a Week 11 clash at home against the Buccaneers.

Wonnum entered the league's concussion protocol during the Lions' Week 8 win over the Vikings. He was held out of Detroit's Week 9 win over Miami, but Wonnum has cleared protocol after passing an evaluation by an independent neurologist. His return bolsters the Lions' rotational depth on the defensive line alongside Aidan Hutchinson, Tyler Lacy and Derrick Moore.

Williams played every single defensive snap in Week 10 and finished tied for the second-most tackles on the Packers behind Isaiah McDuffie (10). Williams has recorded at least eight stops in three of his last four outings and is up to 84 tackles (50 solo), including 1.0 sacks, eight pass defenses (including three interceptions) and a fumble recovery through 10 regular-season games. He is well on track to surpass 100 tackles for a second consecutive year.

McKinney picked off a deep pass from Kirk Cousins intended for Tai Felton late in the second quarter, although the Packers' offense failed to turn that takeaway into points before the end of the half. McKinney has three picks over his last two outings and is up to a league-leading six interceptions. The veteran safety is up to 44 tackles (25 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and seven pass defenses through 10 regular-season games.

Jacobs sustained a fractured right ring finger in the Packers' Nov. 8 win over the Patriots and underwent surgery this past Friday, with the procedure carrying a projected recovery timeline of 2-to-3 weeks. The veteran running back sat out Sunday's 30-10 win over the Vikings, but that could end up being the extent of his absence, as a well-timed Week 11 bye gives him a shot at returning at the short end of his estimated recovery timetable. Kaleb Johnson stepped up as Green Bay's top option out of the backfield while Jacobs has been sidelined for most of the past two games, carrying 24 times for 110 yards and a touchdown between those contests.

As he's been doing since making his season debut in Week 6, Williams operated as the Packers' third receiver against Minnesota. He logged 20 offensive snaps and ran 16 routes on 37 dropbacks. Williams has yet to hit 50 receiving yards in any of his five games this season and has no real fantasy appeal in 12-team fantasy leagues. He's well behind Matthew Golden, Christian Watson and Tucker Kraft in the order for touches and targets.

It was Brooks' first action since Week 4 after spending five games on injured reserve with a high-ankle sprain. With Josh Jacobs (finger) inactive against Minnesota, Brooks led the backfield with 26 offensive snaps in Week 10, but it didn't translate to touches or opportunities to handle the football. With Kaleb Johnson and MarShawn Lloyd also involved, it's difficult to pinpoint any of these three as reliable fantasy options despite Jacobs' absence.

After Green Bay was shut out in the first half, Sturdivant's first career touchdown came in the third quarter from 32 yards out, and it went down as the Packers' lone touchdown of the afternoon. Sturdivant played just nine offensive snaps as the fourth receiver and would need more than one injury ahead of him on the depth chart to be relevant in fantasy.

Smack pushed a 53-yard field-goal try wide right in the first quarter before later converting a 40-yard attempt in the final seconds of the third quarter. The rookie has now gone 15-for-21 on field-goal tries, including 3-for-4 from 50-plus yards, while making 21 of 24 extra-point attempts over 10 contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

Cisse did not return to Sunday's contest after exiting the game during the first quarter with a rib injury. Coach Matt LaFleur says the cornerback is "fine," and it appears Cisse will return to practice after the Packers' Week 11 bye.

The Packers' decision to rule Moore out with an ankle injury in the Week 10 loss to the Vikings was a precautionary move after the 26-year-old made his first appearance since returning from injured reserve. It's unclear if the fifth-year pro will be sidelined for any coming games, but Savion Williams and Matthew Golden will likely act as primary return options if Moore misses any time.

Since opening Parsons' 21-day practice window Nov. 4, the Packers have seemingly targeted their Nov. 25 matchup with the Rams in Week 12 for the star pass rusher's 2026 debut. That plan doesn't appear to have changed while Parsons has been a limited participant in practice for the past two weeks, but he'll likely need to start practicing in full during Week 12 prep before the Packers give him the green light to play. If Parsons does in fact gain clearance to play against the Rams, he could be operating with a restricted snap count in what would mark his first game action since tearing his left ACL on Dec. 14, 2025.

Down 20 points with four minutes remaining in the fourth quarter and with starting quarterback Jordan Love having already taken eight sacks on the afternoon, the Packers opted to turn to Taylor to direct the offense for their final possession of the day. All three of Taylor's appearances on the season have now come late in blowout wins or losses, and his opportunities are likely to remain limited to garbage-time situations so long as Love is healthy.

With Josh Jacobs (finger) sidelined, Green Bay turned to the trio of Lloyd, Kaleb Johnson and Chris Brooks in the backfield. Johnson led the team with 10 carries and 42 total yards despite not getting any targets. Meanwhile, Lloyd turned his seven touches into 39 yards, and Brooks tallied just three yards on his three touches. Green Bay is on bye during the coming week, but Jacobs may still miss the team's next game, which will take place Wednesday, Nov. 25, against the Rams. If that's the case, Lloyd will likely work as part of a shared backfield again, which isn't great for his fantasy outlook.

The former Steeler led the Packers' backfield in totes and rushing yards, with MarShawn Lloyd chipping in 39 scrimmage yards on seven touches. Johnson has produced modest but decent numbers over the last two games, averaging a 4.6 YPC on 24 carries as the top early-down option for Green Bay. Josh Jacobs (finger) could return after the team's Week 11 bye, but if he isn't cleared, Johnson could find himself atop the depth chart again in Week 12 against the Rams.

The tight end's numbers reflected how much time his quarterback had to look downfield, as Jordan Love got sacked eight times in the rout. Kraft has been held to just one catch in back-to-back games, and he heads into a Week 11 bye with a 37-370-3 line on 56 targets through 10 games, with the Rams as the next opponent on the horizon in Week 12.

The second-year wideout was the only Packer to have much success on offense, leading the team in catches, targets and receiving yards. Golden has reached 70 yards in three straight games and five of the last six, and he heads into a Week 11 bye with a 58-853-5 line on 101 targets through 10 contests. His next chance to add to those numbers will come in Week 12 against the Rams.

The Packers' passing game was stifled as the Vikings sacked Jordan Love eight times, giving him little time to find receivers like Watson. The 37 yards were a season low for the fifth-year wideout, while the three grabs tied for his lowest volume of 2026. Watson will take a 52-916-7 line on 79 targets through 10 contests into a Week 11 bye before facing the Rams in Week 12.

The 28-year-old QB came into the game having been sacked just 17 times in his first nine games of the season, but Minnesota brought Love down eight times Sunday. Despite that onslaught, he was able to find J. Michael Sturdivant for a 32-yard TD in the third quarter to salvage his line slightly. It was the first time since Week 6 that Love had failed to throw multiple touchdowns, and just the second time all season. He'll get a Week 11 bye to heal up from Sunday's pummeling before facing Myles Garrett and the Rams in Week 12.

Melton exited Sunday's game because of a thigh injury, and he will not be cleared to return to the contest. Skyy Moore (ankle) will also not return, so Savion Williams and Matthew Golden will operate as the top return options on kickoffs and punts.

Glover's practice reps were limited during Week 10 prep due to a knee injury that prevented him from playing against the Patriots in Week 9. The third-year pro was cleared by medical staff to play Sunday, and he should reclaim his starting role at right guard from Laken Tomlinson.

Van Ness upgraded to limited in Friday's practice while dealing with a back injury. The weakside linebacker has recovered enough to suit up for Sunday's contest against a Vikings team that is also fighting for the NFC North title.

Bullard was upgraded to a limited participant in Friday's practice and is questionable ahead of Sunday's contest. The starting slot cornerback is all set to suit up, seemingly having overcome his ankle injury in time for a heavyweight NFC North bout with the Vikings.

With Woody Marks (concussion) inactive, Demercado played the complementary role behind lead back David Montgomery, who rushed 26 times for 107 yards in his return from a multi-week groin injury. Demercado was picked up off waivers from Dallas last month.

The wideout had one of his more productive games of the season before being injured, as he caught both of his targets for 40 yards and a touchdown. His 40 yards were the second-most he's produced in a game this season. Boutte is up to 21 grabs for 359 yards and three touchdowns on 31 targets across 10 games in 2026.

Hutchinson played 54 of 66 offensive snaps, second at wide receiver on the team behind Nico Collins' 59, and the former has been operating as the Texans' WR2 in terms of playing time for the last several weeks. By not scoring a touchdown Thursday night, Hutchinson snapped his personal three-game touchdown streak. For the season, he has 30 catches for 358 yards and three scores on 57 targets. He's on pace to set new career highs across the board.

Klein surprisingly outpaced veteran position mates Dalton Schultz and Foster Moreau on the night, and the rookie second-round pick, whose only other career reception coming in was a 16-yard grab in Week 1, added his first career touchdown on a 13-yard catch in the third quarter. Given Klein had been a complete non-factor coming into the night, it's difficult to predict whether Thursday's production will have any carryover to a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Schultz had a minimal role on a night when C.J. Stroud threw for a modest 194 yards and recorded completions to nine different targets. The veteran tight end now has consecutive one-catch, 11-yard tallies after recording multiple receptions in each of his first eight games of the season, and Schultz's production will remain hard to trust heading into a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29.

The speedy wideout finished tied for second in receptions for the Texans on a night when C.J. Stroud recorded completions to nine different targets overall. Dell has played an effective complementary role since making his return from a gruesome 2024 knee injury in Week 7, as he now has an 11-196-1 line and four catches of 20-plus yards across 18 targets heading into a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Stroud's night got off to a rocky start when a deflected pass resulted in an interception on the Texans' opening drive, but the red-hot signal-caller was near perfect from that point forward. The 2023 first-round pick went on to toss three touchdown passes for the second straight game and multiple scores for the fifth consecutive contest overall. Stroud connected with Nico Collins (42 yards), Kayshon Boutte (24 yards) and Marlin Klein (13 yards) for his trio of scoring strikes, and he'll take a sparkling 22:4 TD:INT into a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Facing a Colts defense down both Sauce Gardner (calf) and Charvarius Ward (knee), Collins looked primed for a big night early when he recorded a 42-yard touchdown grab to cap off Houston's second possession. However, C.J. Stroud proceeded to spread the ball around to nine different targets overall, leading to Collins tying his second-lowest reception tally and posting his third-lowest yardage total of the season. However, the star wideout did extend his touchdown streak to three games, and he'll next take aim at what has been an inconsistent Ravens secondary in a Week 12 home matchup on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Making his return from a four-game absence due to a groin injury, Montgomery functioned as the clear lead back with Woody Marks (concussion) unavailable. The former put together the best rushing yardage total of his brief Texans tenure, handling his highest number of carries since Week 4 of his 2023 debut campaign with the Lions. Montgomery also was encouragingly involved in a complementary role in the passing game, and he'll now have some extra time to recover from Thursday's workload ahead of a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29. However, if Marks is able to clear concussion protocol ahead of that contest, Montgomery will see his touch count take a hit.

The Texans announced Rutledge's injury in the waning moments of the contest, but he had been in the medical tent well before that time. Febechi Nwaiwu took over at left guard following Rutledge's departure. With Houston not set to play again until Sunday, Nov. 29, against Baltimore, Rutledge will look to recover from the stinger in time to suit up.

Brown left Thursday's contest after suffering a back injury, but he was able to check back in with the Texans' field goal team in the second quarter. With that said, veteran Braden Smith was still working as Houston's right tackle when the first half of Thursday's game ended.

Rankins sustained an apparent ankle injury during the second quarter of Thursday's contest, and he was able to walk gingerly to the sideline under his own power. In his absence, rookie second-rounder Kayden McDonald figures to see an increase in snaps on the defensive line.

Braswell suffered an injury in kick coverage on the opening kickoff and was promptly carted off the field with his right leg in an air cast, per James Boyd of The Athletic. The Texans will have to try to find a way to replace his production on special teams.

Teller was unavailable in Week 10 against the Browns due to an illness, and he'll be sidelined in Week 11 by a back injury. In his absence, rookie fourth-rounder Febechi Nwaiwu projects as the Texans' top option off the bench at guard.

The linebacker suffered the injury in Week 1, returned for Week 10 and then carried a questionable tag into this contest, but he appears ready to play through the injury for the second consecutive game. Hummel logged two tackles (one solo) across 21 special-teams snaps against the Browns last week.

The cornerback was activated from injured reserve earlier in the day Thursday and will be making his first appearance since Week 4. Smith played just seven defensive snaps across the first four games of the season.

The Texans are reinserting Reed Blankenship in the starting lineup after he returned from a broken hand and concussion Sunday against the Browns to play only two defensive snaps. Stewart recorded 14 tackles (four solo) in the loss but gave up a long reception to Jerry Jeudy in coverage. The Texans are looking for answers to get their defense back near the top of the league.

The safety missed two games with a broken hand and concussion before returning last Sunday against the Browns. He played just two defensive snaps versus Cleveland and logged 12 on special teams, but the Texans are swapping Blankenship back in at safety ahead of M.J. Stewart. Blankenship has 47 tackles (26 solo) and three pass breakups, including an interception, across seven appearances this season.

Lassiter did not participate in Tuesday' walkthrough due to a wrist issue. The cornerback sandwiched the DNP between two full sessions and has been cleared to play in Thursday night's contest. If Lassiter must see fewer snaps in the game as he manages the issue, Ja'Marcus Ingram could see the field opposite Derek Stingley.

Hunter will now miss consecutive contests due to a hamstring injury he sustained during Week 10 prep. The pass rusher was unable to practice during Week 11 prep as he continues to deal with the issue. Jadeveon Clowney is set to start at defensive end opposite Will Anderson for Thursday's AFC South showdown.

Jordan missed all three Week 11 practice sessions due to an injury and an illness. The tight end will miss a second straight game, this time with two separate issues as opposed to the finger injury that plagued him ahead of Week 10. Marlin Klein or Cade Stover is set to be the No. 3 tight end behind Dalton Schultz and Foster Moreau for Thursday night's contest.

Treadwell played a position-high 40 of 50 offensive snaps but continues to run wind sprints in an offense that doesn't throw the ball down the field. Through 11 games this season, Treadwell has just 19 catches for 239 yards and one touchdown on 33 targets.

Gould was the rather unlikely leader in receiving yards for the Colts on the night, with a team-high 31-yard catch playing a big role in getting him there. The 2024 fifth-round pick has seen an expanded role in the wake of the trades of Josh Downs and Keenan Allen, and for as long as Alec Pierce (IR, heel) is sidelined, Gould could function as one of Indianapolis' top downfield threats for either Daniel Jones, Anthony Richardson or Riley Leonard.

The talented tight end's production continued to suffer collateral damage from Daniel Jones' poor play, but Warren did provide a useful gain on his one catch. The 2025 first-round pick now has recorded Thursday's yardage total or less in three of the last four games, but Warren's outlook may change if Jones, who James Boyd of The Athletic reports head coach Shane Steichen wouldn't rule out demoting when asked after the game, is replaced by Anthony Richardson or Riley Leonard under center.

Jones' final line underscores how ineffective he was for the fifth straight game, once again finishing well under 200 passing yards, extending his streak of games with at least one interception to six and taking a safety early in the second half. Although the 3-8 Colts don't have any realistic designs on the postseason, James Boyd of The Athletic reports Colts head coach Shane Steichen said, "I'll evaluate everything," when asked if he'll consider benching Jones ahead of a Week 12 home matchup against the Giants on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Taylor put some distance between himself and promising rookie backfield mate Seth McGowan in terms of workload, as the former outpaced his teammate in carries by an 11-3 margin, even with the latter exiting before halftime with a hamstring injury. However, the extra opportunity was a moot point, as Taylor couldn't find any space to operate as either a runner or receiver. Daniel Jones' mediocre play under center certainly isn't helping the ground attack's cause, and Taylor now has recorded less than 50 rushing yards in three of the last four contests. The star running back will have some additional time to prepare for a relatively favorable Week 12 home matchup against the Giants on Sunday, Nov. 29.

McGowan was injured just before halftime while returning a kickoff. He was deemed questionable to return at the beginning of the third quarter and subsequently was ruled out shortly thereafter. The rookie running back gained seven yards on three carries and caught his only target for one yard before exiting while adding 117 yards on three kickoff returns. Jonathan Taylor should continue to get most of the work at running back for the Colts for the rest of the game, and DJ Giddens should handle whatever backfield snaps that Taylor doesn't get.

Leonard will retain the same role he's played for Indianapolis all season in Week 11, being ready on the sidelines in case both Daniel Jones and Anthony Richardson are knocked out of action. There have been some holes in the Texans' pass defense through their first nine games of the campaign, but it's unclear whether the Colts have pass-catching personnel capable of taking advantage.
Rhodes is the team's long snapper. He missed last Sunday's win over Miami.

The second-year defensive back was responsible for perhaps the biggest play of the game, as his strip sack of the Dolphins' Kyle McCord early in the third quarter led to a fumble recovery in the end zone by teammate Adetomiwa Adebawore. Walley was named the AFC Defensive Player of the Week for his big performance.

Allen led the Colts in tackles Sunday, and he got to Dolphins quarterback Kyle McCord for an eight-yard loss late in the fourth quarter. Allen also picked off McCord earlier in the fourth, although the play was nullified by an illegal contact penalty by Colts defensive back Kenneth Harris. Allen has logged at least 10 tackles in each of his last three outings, and he has accumulated 34 tackles (12 solo), including 2.0 sacks, and two pass defenses across seven regular-season games.

Even with Josh Downs and Keenan Allen being sent out at the Nov. 10 trade deadline, Dulin's 13 offensive snaps were fourth-most among Colts wide receivers behind Laquon Treadwell (52), Deion Burks (34) and Anthony Gould (32). Dulin did connect on a 30-yard pass from Daniel Jones late in the second quarter, which was a pivotal part of a nine-play, 92-yard drive that ended with a seven-yard touchdown catch by Treadwell. Dulin has logged catches of 55 and 30 yards in each of his last two outings, and he could be the Colts' WR3 for Thursday's AFC South tilt against the Texans if Gould is not cleared to play due to a toe injury.

With Josh Downs and Keenan Allen being shipped off at the Nov. 10 deadline, the Colts turned to Burks, Laquon Treadwell and Anthony Gould to serve as the top wideouts for Week 10. Burks' 34 offensive snaps were a season high and second among the team's wide receivers, but the rookie seventh-rounder failed to record a catch for the fifth time in 10 games, with one of his intended passes from Daniel Jones being intercepted midway through the second quarter. Gould is working through a toe injury, so Burks could step into a bigger role on offense against the Texans on Thursday.

Carlies hurt his neck in Week 9 against Dallas and didn't practice at all last week before being ruled out for Sunday's win over the Dolphins. Now that he's landed on IR, the third-year linebacker will need to miss at least the Colts' next four games. Austin Ajiake and West Weeks will likely soak up the rotational defensive snaps that Carlies had been getting.

A spot on the 53-man roster opened up when Indianapolis placed linebacker Jaylon Carlies (neck) on IR, and the team elected to give Watkins the opening. The veteran wideout was elevated for Sunday's Week 10 win over Miami, but he didn't end up playing. With that said, there could be an opportunity for Watkins to garner some work in the passing game after Indianapolis traded Josh Downs to the Chiefs and Keenan Allen to the 49ers last week. Watkins last logged regular-season NFL action in 2023, when he caught 15 of 21 targets for 142 yards and a touchdown over nine games with the Eagles.

Shrader sole field-goal attempt was a 51-yard make in the third quarter of Sunday's contest. The kicker moves to 23-for-25 on field-goal attempts and 19-for-20 on PATs through 10 games of the 2026 regular season.

Giddens barely saw the field during Sunday's win, and his two offensive snaps were well behind fellow running backs Jonathan Taylor (40) and Seth McGowan (17). Giddens -- a fifth-round pick of the Colts in the 2025 NFL Draft -- has seen little playing time since making his 2026 regular-season debut in Week 8 against the Jaguars. His role will likely stay minimal for Week 11 against the Texans on Thursday.

Davis-Gaither was already ruled out for Sunday's game against Miami in what would be his second consecutive missed contest due to a knee injury. Now that he's been placed on IR, the seventh-year pro will be required to miss at least four games, so his next chance to play is Week 15 against the Titans on Sunday, Dec. 20.

Key missed the Colts' last five games while on injured reserve due to a hamstring injury that he sustained in Week 4 against the Commanders. He was cleared to return to practice Wednesday and logged a trio of full sessions, which gave the Colts the confidence to activate the veteran defensive lineman from IR ahead of Sunday's contest. Prior to his IR stint, Key posted eight tackles (three solo), including 0.5 sacks, and one forced fumble in four regular-season games.

Tuten did not get any work in Thursday after being limited at Wednesday's practice, but Coen's comments suggest he could be back on the field Friday. Tuten was listed as either limited or as a non-participant the last eight times the Jaguars released an injury report but has not missed a game, so while his status is up in the air there is reason to believe he will be out there Sunday. Tuten's status for Week 11 will officially be revealed when the Jaguars release their next injury report later Friday.

Allen is one of three Jaguars running backs on the Week 11 injury report, with Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) and Chris Rodriguez (hand) also tending to health concerns. After being listed as a non-participant Thursday, Tuten appears to be more at risk of sitting out Sunday against the Giants than either Allen or Rodriguez, both of whom have been limited in the Jaguars' first two Week 11 practices.

Though Rodriguez has been limited in both of the team's first two Week 11 practices, the Jaguars haven't indicated that the running back's availability for Sunday's game against the Giants is in any real peril. In fact, Rodriguez could be headed for his most substantial workload of the season Sunday, as Bhayshul Tuten's (ankle/foot) may be at risk of sitting out that contest after downgrading from limited participation Wednesday to no activity during Thursday's practice.

Meyers had his reps capped for a second straight practice, but if he can maintain limited activity or upgrade to full participation Friday, he should be on track to play Sunday against the Giants. The veteran slot receiver has yet to miss a game this season, recording 29 receptions for 408 yards and two touchdowns on 43 targets through nine appearances.

Striggow was forced to check out of Sunday's game at Tennessee after suffering a blow to the head, and he's now dealing with a concussion as the Jaguars begin their Week 11 preparations. If he's able to upgrade to full participation at practice Thursday or Friday, it could signal he's close to clearing concussion protocol ahead of Sunday's game against the Giants.

Johnson returns to limited practice participation after completing Week 10 without any injury designation. The safety overcame an ankle injury to suit up for the Jaguars' Week 9 win over the Ravens but appears to have aggrevated the recovering area in the team's Week 10 win over the Titans. Johnson will need to continue to log limited or full practices during the remaining two Week 11 prep sessions for a chance to avoid any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Giants.

Walker injured his ribs in Week 8 against the Colts, but the fifth-year pro was cleared to play in each of the Jaguars' last two games. Unless his practice participation decreases over the next two days, Walker should be good to go for Sunday's road game against the Giants. The 2022 first-rounder has 22 tackles (10 solo), including 3.0 sacks, and two pass defenses through nine regular-season games.

Jonah Monheim will draw the start at center in place of Hainsey, who exited this past Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans due to a knee sprain, per Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com. According to Fowler, Hainsey's knee injury isn't considered season-ending, but the veteran lineman is viewed as week-to-week and could be a candidate for injured reserve.

Sunday was the third time in nine regular-season games that Oluokun played every single defensive snap and the second time that he reached double-digit tackles. His nine solo stops were a season high and most in a game since Week 1 of the 2024 season. Oluokun has accumulated 44 tackles (30 solo), including 2.0 sacks, over his last five outings.

Little was able to make four field-goal tries for the second straight week, converting attempts from 46, 48, 36 and 40 yards in the contest. The kicker has now gone 18-for-20 on field-goal attempts, including 4-for-6 from 50-plus yards, over nine contests during the 2026 campaign.

Fifty-six of Hunter's 62 snaps Sunday came on defense, and that's where he made his biggest impact with a diving interception on a Cam Ward pass intended for Elic Ayomanor, and the Jaguars offense converted that takeaway into a field goal 10 plays later. Hunter's impact on both sides of the ball has been undeniable: he has 28 catches (on 45 targets) for 298 yards and a touchdown, along with 36 tackles (24 solo) and seven pass defenses (including three interceptions) through nine regular-season games. The Jaguars will hit the road for Week 11 against the Giants on Nov. 22.

Cameron gave the Jaguars a 14-point lead early in the fourth quarter when he hauled in a 25-yard touchdown pass from Trevor Lawrence. It was the rookie wideout's third touchdown of the campaign but his first since Week 3. Cameron's 67 receiving yards marked a career high, while his three receptions tied the most he's had as a pro. Cameron's propensity for finding the end zone (his three TDs have come on just 12 total catches) is appealing, but at this point he isn't getting enough volume to be a reliable week-to-week fantasy asset.

The three catches tied his season high, while the four targets represented his biggest volume since Week 2. The Jaguars' decision not to deal Thomas at the trade deadline remains a curious one, as the third-year wideout simply doesn't have a significant role in Liam Coen's offense and might not step into one even if someone like Parker Washington got injured -- Josh Cameron was more productive Sunday on three targets and caught one of Trevor Lawrence's three TDs. Thomas will take a 13-146-2 line on 26 targets over nine games into a Week 11 tilt against the Giants.

The 152 receiving yards were a new career high for Washington, and the fourth-year WR highlighted his big day with a two-yard TD toss from Trevor Lawrence in the first quarter to open the scoring. It's Washington's second game this season with 100-plus yards, and he'll take a 36-645-6 line on 64 targets through nine contests into a Week 11 tilt against the Giants.

It was another huge performance from the 27-year-old QB, as Lawrence set a new season high in passing yards and threw at least three TDs for the fifth time in nine games to begin the year. He spread the ball around again, as seven different Jaguars caught multiple passes and Parker Washington, Josh Cameron and Brenton Strange were all on the other end of scores. Lawrence will take a sharp 21:5 TD:INT into a Week 11 clash with the Giants.

The Jaguars keep blowing out their opponents, and Strange contributed a three-yard touchdown Sunday but was otherwise not heard from much, as Parker Washington dog-walked the Titans' secondary for 7-152-1 receiving on nine targets. Strange's touchdown grab was his first since Week 1. He remans a locked-in TE1 for fantasy, as he is playing virtually every snap in an elite offense.
Green's 21-day practice window opened Nov. 11. The Jaguars' defensive end logged three consecutive full sessions in his return to practice but was ultimately deemed not ready to suit up for Week 10.

Bolton popped up on the Chiefs' injury report with a shin issue Wednesday, but it doesn't look like it was anything serious. He's fifth in the league in total tackles (89) going into a Week 11 matchup versus a pass-happy Cardinals offense.

Walker is looking extremely unlikely to play Sunday against a Cardinals team that Kansas City should handle with ease at home. The Chiefs have a quick Week 12 turnaround against the Bills on Thanksgiving, and it may make sense to let Walker rest for another week in preparation for that contest, especially after rookie Emmett Johnson showed in Week 10 against Atlanta that he's more than capable of carrying the torch in the backfield. Fantasy players need to be prepared to be without Walker for at least one more week.

Norman-Lott was removed from the PUP list prior to the expiration of his 21-day practice window. He was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, and his participation over the next two days will determine whether he'll make his 2026 regular-season debut against the Cardinals on Sunday. Norman-Lott is in the final stages of his recovery from a torn ACL that he sustained in October of 2025.

Woods has missed the Chiefs' last two contests with a neck injury he sustained in the team's Week 8 loss to the Broncos. The rookie first-rounder now starts Week 11 prep as a full participant, meaning he will likely suit up for Sunday's contest against the Cardinals as a rotational option for the Chiefs' defensive line.

Smith entered the league's concussion protocol during the Chiefs' Week 10 win over the Falcons. Even if he practices over the coming days, he would need to clear protocol in order to be available for Sunday's game against the Cardinals. Mike Caliendo would likely start at right guard if Smith doesn't play.

Moore did not play against the Falcons in Week 10 due to an ankle injury he sustained against the Jets in Week 9. He'll have two more chances to practice in at least a limited capacity, but if he cannot play against the Cardinals on Sunday, then Joshua Ezeudu would likely start at right tackle for a second consecutive game.

Wiley was carted to the locker room in the first quarter of the Chiefs' Week 10 win over the Falcons with an ankle injury. The tight end will now be on IR as he nurses his fractured ankle until at least the latter part of the regular season. Travis Kelce, Noah Gray and Jake Briningstool are now the only tight ends on the Chiefs' active roster.

Ott was unable to play against the Falcons in Week 10 due to a hamstring injury. However, the undrafted rookie out of Oklahoma was cleared to practice in full Wednesday, so he should be available for Sunday's home game against the Cardinals. If Kenneth Walker (groin) cannot play in Week 11, then Ott would have the opportunity to serve as the Chiefs' RB2 behind rookie fifth-rounder Emmett Johnson.

During this past Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons, Kelce exited for a brief spell in the first half after injuring his ankle, but he ultimately returned to the contest. In addition to the ankle issue, Kelce may have tweaked his calf at some point in Week 10, but head coach Andy Reid indicated prior to Wednesday's practice that the veteran tight end is "doing well" in his recovery from the injuries, per Charles Goldman of AtoZSports.com. His ability to take every rep for the Chiefs' first Week 11 session suggests his status for Sunday's game againt the Cardinals isn't in any peril.

Tranquill finished tied for the team lead in tackles with fellow linebacker Nick Bolton in Week 10, notching at least nine takedowns for the third time in four weeks after not having reached that mark in any of the team's first five games of the year. On the season, Tranquill has now produced 75 total tackles (39 solo), two passes defensed and a fumble recovery over nine contests so far.

Williams was able to register at least five takedowns for the third time this season, and his biggest moment of the game came in the fourth quarter when he intercepted a deep pass from Falcons quarterback Michael Penix. The interception was his second of the year, and he has now compiled 41 total tackles (23 solo) and 11 passes defensed over nine contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

Briningstool connected with Patrick Mahomes for a 20-yard reception midway through the first quarter but didn't record another reception. The 23-year-old tight end has exactly one catch in each of his past three games. That's not enough production to warrant fantasy consideration, but Briningstool is at least showing growth as a pass catcher, as he had just one catch on two targets over his first six contests of the campaign.
Butker did not attempt a field goal in the contest, as the Chiefs solely scored touchdowns. He now moves to 27-for-28 on PATs in 2026 as he continues to struggle to hold onto the starting kicker job.

Gray was unable to reel in multiple passes for the second straight week after he had at least two catches in each of the team's previous five games prior to Week 9. The tight end did play a season-high 53 offensive snaps with Travis Kelce being limited to just 18 snaps on offense as a result of an ankle injury. If Kelce is forced to be limited or even miss the team's Week 11 matchup with Arizona, Gray would stand to operate as the team's primary tight end in his place.

The wideout played just 17 of 64 offensive snaps against Atlanta and ran only seven pass routes on Patrick Mahomes' 38 dropbacks. Armstrong was tasked with blocking duties on 10 of his snaps. He still managed to catch his first career touchdown in the fourth quarter with the game already well out of hand. Armstrong is not on the fantasy radar.

The rookie wideout scored his first career touchdown by beating the cornerback on a stutter-go for a 39-yard touchdown in the third quarter. With Josh Downs still getting comfortable and learning the offense following Tuesday's acquisition from the Colts, Allen maintained a significant role on offense, playing 22 of 64 offensive snaps. Once Downs progresses from the 10 snaps he played against Atlanta, it will be interesting to see if Allen can push Xavier Worthy (zero catches on three targets across 56 snaps on Sunday) for a larger piece of the outside receiver role in Kansas City's offense.

Worthy ran a team-high 37 routes on Patrick Mahomes' 38 dropbacks, but on a day Mahomes targeted nine different players, Worthy was the only one to not record a catch. With Josh Downs now in the fold and working to get comfortable in the offense, Worthy's role will likely only continue to shrink. On just eight routes in his team debut Sunday, Downs posted a 4-53-1 receiving line on five targets. Worthy hasn't produced that many fantasy points in a game all season. He's waiver-wire fodder in 12-team redraft leagues.

Making his Chiefs debut following three days of practice after arriving via trade from the Colts on Tuesday, Downs looked right at home in the Patrick Mahomes-led offense. The young wideout fully capitalized on the upgrade he saw at quarterback, finishing third in receptions, receiving yards and targets right out of the gate and adding his second touchdown of the season on a difficult 18-yard catch just before halftime. Downs' immediate chemistry with Mahomes is highly welcome news for fantasy managers, and he'll aim to carry the momentum over into a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Cardinals next Sunday.

Drawing his first career start due to Kenneth Walker (groin) being sidelined, Johnson put on a pretty convincing impression of his star teammate. Not only did Johnson just get himself over the century mark in rushing yards, but he finished as the team leader in receptions and targets while checking in as the runner-up in receiving yards. Johnson struck from 12 and six yards out for his two receiving TDs, underscoring his considerable versatility. If Walker is unable to garner active status for next Sunday's Week 11 matchup against the Cardinals, the Chiefs' ground attack will remain in good hands with Johnson.

Rice led the Chiefs in receiving yards and finished second in receptions and targets on a prolific afternoon for the Chiefs' air attack. Rice didn't get in on the scoring fun of a five-touchdown day for Patrick Mahomes, but he still eclipsed 80 receiving yards for the third time this season and first time since Week 3. Rice's level of involvement was encouraging given the debuting Josh Downs drew five targets, keeping the former's prospects bright for a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Cardinals next Sunday.

Taking advantage of a controlled environment and a fast track at Mercedes-Benz Stadium -- not to mention the presence of the debuting Josh Downs -- Mahomes repeatedly exploited the vulnerabilities of the Falcons defense throughout the afternoon. The legendary signal-caller showed no ill effects from the elbow injury that he'd suffered in Week 9, and he connected with Emmett Johnson (12, six yards), Downs (18 yards), Cyrus Allen (39 yards) and Andrew Armstrong (43 yards) for his quintet of touchdown passes. Mahomes now has multiple scoring strikes and zero interceptions in three straight games, and Sunday's five TD tosses represented a new season high. Mahomes will take 2,385 passing yards and a 19:4 TD:INT into a Week 11 home matchup against the Cardinals next Sunday.

Delane has been given the green light to return from a two-game absence due to a shoulder injury. The rookie first-rounder will likely return to his starting role at outside cornerback opposite Nohl Williams, while Kristian Fulton and Christian Roland-Wallace provide depth at the position.

Bowers missed Wednesday's practice, but his return a day later, albeit in a limited fashion, is a positive sign as Sunday's game against the Broncos approaches. Head coach Klint Kubiak noted Wednesday that the star tight end doesn't need to practice this week in order to play this weekend, per Sam Warren of The Athletic, but Bowers already has cleared his first hurdle toward that end by virtue of his participation in Thursday's session.

An ankle injury has sidelined Booker for each of the Raiders' last two games. However, his full session Wednesday indicates that he's recovered from his injury and on track to play in Sunday's AFC West tilt against the Broncos. Booker has accumulated 13 tackles (nine solo) across seven regular-season games.

Hemingway is currently dealing with a stinger, making his status for Sunday's matchup versus Denver uncertain. With Folorunso Fatukasi (toe) also dealing with an injury, the Raiders could find themselves shorthanded along the defensive line against the Broncos, as Thomas Booker is the only healthy defensive end currently on the active roster.

Fatukasi logged 31 defensive snaps in Week 10 versus the Seahawks, but it looks like he might have hurt his toe along the way. He'll probably need to practice in full Thursday or Friday to avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

Paye made an early exit in the second half of Sunday's loss to the Seahawks with a neck injury. The linebacker did not return to the contest, but the issue does not seem to have been serious. Paye is healthy and appears ready to log consistent full practices throughout Week 11 prep.

Thornton is healthy again after sitting out the team's Week 10 loss to the Seahawks due to a back injury. However, it is still unlikely that the 23-year-old plays in Sunday's matchup versus the Broncos, as Thornton had been a healthy scratch every week since returning from injured reserve in late October prior to Week 10.

Gay made both of his two field-goal tries and his only extra-point attempt during Sunday's 21-13 loss versus the Seahawks, but it looks like he might have picked up a hip injury at some point along the way. As long as he can manage a full practice Thursday or Friday, he should still be in a good position to suit up in Week 11 against the Broncos.

Chinn continues to put up consistent tackling numbers, as he's now logged at least seven stops in six straight games. The veteran safety has played all but one of Las Vegas' defensive snaps this season. He's up to 72 tackles, including 1.0 sacks, two pass defenses (including one interception), two forced fumbles and two recovered fumbles through 10 contests.

Walker, Nakobe Dean and Maxx Crosby all had eight tackles Sunday to co-lead the team. Walker added a fumble recovery on the second play of the game that helped set up a Raiders touchdown. The veteran linebacker has remained productive in his first season with Las Vegas following four years in Green Bay. Walker has 80 tackles, including 2.0 sacks, and two recovered fumbles though 10 contests on the campaign.

Dean tied for the team lead in stops with Maxx Crosby and Quay Walker. Nonetheless, the veteran linebacker saw his five-game streak of double-digit tackles come to an end. Dean did contribute his first recovered fumble of the season when he scooped up a ball that was turned over by Seattle QB Drew Lock in the fourth quarter. Dean is tied with Broncos linebacker Alex Singleton for the NFL lead with 107 tackles, though Denver has played one fewer game.

Crosby tied for the team lead with his season-high eight stops. Among those tackles, four went for a loss, including a fourth-quarter sack of Drew Lock. After registering just a half-sack over six games from Week 2 to Week 7, Crosby has since finished with exactly 1.0 sacks in each of his past three contests. He's at 5.0 sacks overall through 10 games as he seeks a fifth NFL campaign with double-digit sacks.

Bech was the favorite target of rookie first-overall pick Fernando Mendoza, who was making his first career start Sunday after the Raiders shipped Kirk Cousins to the Vikings at the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Bech's seven targets were a season high, but he mustered only two catches for his efforts, and he failed to connect on each of the last four passes he saw from Mendoza in the fourth quarter. The volume appears to be there for Bech, and he could take on a larger role offensively in Week 11 against the Broncos on Nov. 22 if star tight end Brock Bowers (ankle) is unable to play.

Young has suited up in each of the Raiders' 10 games this season, but he's been deployed almost exclusively on special teams. He's seen single-digit snaps on offense in five straight games and has posted a collective 2-36-0 receiving line on three targets on the campaign.

Making his first NFL start, No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza was under siege throughout the afternoon, as a ferocious Seahawks defense sacked him six times and limited him to just 143 passing yards on 29 attempts. As a result, Nailor and the Raiders' other pass catchers were held quiet, with running back Ashton Jeanty (four receptions for 46 yards) being the only Las Vegas player to top two catches and 25 receiving yards. Though Mendoza will get some more favorable matchups over the Raiders' final seven games, Nailor will be difficult to count on for production. Even while Kirk Cousins served as the starting quarterback for Las Vegas before being traded to the Vikings last week, Nailor was limited to just 14 receptions for 122 yards and one touchdown on 28 targets through eight appearances.

Since earning seven touches in a Week 5 blowout loss to the Patriots, Laube has been an afterthought on offense. He's played just eight total offense snaps in the Raiders' ensuing five games, and Sunday marked the first time all season that he was limited exclusively to special teams.

Jack Bech (seven targets) was the only Las Vegas player to see more than four targets in Fernando Mendoza's first career start. The rookie quarterback targeted 10 different players on his 29 attempts. With Kirk Cousins' efficiency off to Minnesota, Mayer is a low-floor TE2 for fantasy, but he could get a bit of a boost if Brock Bowers' ankle injury causes him to miss time.

In Fernando Mendoza's first career start at quarterback, Tucker saw just 6.9 percent of the targets, while Jack Bech led the team with seven looks. Tucker looks like someone who won't be usable in fantasy until he shows some tangible chemistry with the young quarterback.

The Mendoza era in Las Vegas officially kicked off this week following the trade of veteran QB Kirk Cousins to the Vikings, and the rookie first overall pick unsurprisingly flashed at times while also stalling numerous drives by taking six sacks overall. On a positive note, Mendoza didn't turn the ball over, and he also recorded his first touchdown as a pro on a 10-yard run on the Raiders' opening offensive possession. He'll seek to build on the initial start of his career next Sunday at Denver.

Aside from a 25-carry outburst in Week 8 at the Jets, Washington has logged 54 rushes along with four catches in nine appearances, which amounts to 6.4 touches per game. Despite that number, he continues to eat into the overall backfield picture, as lead runner Ashton Jeanty failed to tally double-digit rushes for a fourth straight contest Sunday. Washington should retain a modest role alongside Jeanty next Sunday at Denver.

After reaching the 10-carry threshold in each of the first six games of the season, Jeanty has failed to do so in four straight contests, and he also has fallen shy of 30 rushing yards in six consecutive outings. Rookie RB Mike Washington continued to split the backfield with Jeanty in Week 10, turning his nine touches into 27 yards from scrimmage. Considering recent trends, Jeanty is difficult to trust for consistent production without a boost in work.
The tight end remains in concussion protocol and looks like he'll miss Sunday's game against the Jets. If so, Oronde Gadsden and David Njoku would step in to handle most of the tight-end duties.

McConkey, who was inactive in Week 10 and didn't log any snaps during Week 9 action due to back spasms, also was limited Wednesday. Per Noah Furtado of The Athletic, the wideout was seen at Thursday's practice in a non-contact jersey, as he continues to manage his back issue. With that in mind, unless McConkey is able work fully Friday, he'll likely carry an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets.

In a game where Ravens quarterback Jacoby Brissett dropped back 51 times, there were no shortage of opportunities for the Chargers to rush the passer, and Tomlinson came away with the best single-game sack total of his nine-plus year career so far. He has taken on a larger role on the defensive line than 2025 third-rounder Jamaree Caldwell in recent weeks, and only Teair Tart played as many snaps on the Chargers' defensive front as Tomlinson did (36) in Week 10.

Phillips was in the right place at the right time when a Jacoby Brissett pass bounced off the helmet of rookie wideout Ja'Kobi Lane in the second quarter, and the turnover set up a Chargers touchdown that put the team ahead 17-7. His tackle total was also his highest going back to Week 18 of the 2023 season with the Ravens. With that said, his role in the Chargers' defense is still not big enough to warrant IDP consideration in most formats.

Henley popped up on the injury report Wednesday after compiling 11 tackles (five solo) during the Week 10 win over the Ravens. Marlowe Wax would be in line to start at inside linebacker during Sunday's matchup versus the Jets if Henley ends up being unable to play.

Dicker's longest field goal on the day was only from 38 yards out, but his accuracy played a big part in the Chargers picking up their first win of the season. He hasn't missed a kick since Week 3, but the team's general inability to move the ball consistently keeps him from projecting as a top-tier fantasy option in most formats going into a Week 11 matchup versus the Jets.

Njoku's snap count was predictably capped as he returned from a six-game absence due to a fibula injury that he sustained in Week 2 against the Raiders. His 19 offensive snaps were actually ahead of Oronde Gadsden (12), with Charlie Kolar leading all Chargers tight ends with 41 snaps on offense. With another week under his belt to get back up to speed, Njoku could be more involved in the Chargers' passing attack in Week 11 against the Jets on Sunday.

Gadsden went to the locker room during the first half of Monday's game after being poked in the ye, but the second-year tight end was cleared to return for the second quarter. However, his 12 offensive snaps were his lowest since Week 1 against the Cardinals (10), and that lack of playing time coincided with the return of veteran tight end David Njoku, who missed the Chargers' six prior games while on IR due to a fibula injury. Njoku and Charlie Kolar appear to be the Chargers' top options at tight end, squeezing Gadsden out of the game plan ahead of Week 11 against the Jets on Sunday.

Vidal's 15 offensive snaps were just ahead of Keaton Mitchell's 13, but both running backs took a back seat to Omarion Hampton, who was on the field for 36 of the Chargers' 57 snaps on offense and led the backfield with 22 carries for 105 yards and one touchdown. Vidal's two carries were his fewest since Week 3 against the Bills (one), although his 15-yard catch early in the third quarter set the Chargers up just outside the red zone, with Cameron Dicker connecting on a 34-yard field goal four plays later. Vidal and Mitchell appear to be falling into rotational roles behind Hampton heading into Week 11 against the Jets on Sunday.

One of Mitchell's carries went for 11 yards, but his other two rushes went for minus-five and minus-two yards, and all of those touches came on the same drive in the second quarter. His 13 offensive snaps were third-most among Chargers running backs behind Kimani Vidal (15) and Omarion Hampton (36), and it was Hampton that commanded the majority of backfield touches, finishing with 22 carries for 105 yards and a touchdown. Mitchell has logged four carries or fewer in three of his last four outings, and he'll continue to operate in a rotational role on offense heading into the Chargers' Week 11 home tilt against the Jets on Sunday.

The speedster was poised to see some added involvement with Ladd McConkey (back) sidelined, but that never materialized on a night when 86 of Justin Herbert's 129 passing yards went to Tre' Harris. Johnston's yardage total was a season-low figure, and he's now been limited to one reception in four of the last five games. Johnston's often been able to offset the modest catch totals with big plays, but that clearly wasn't the case Monday night. Johnston will remain a hit-or-miss fantasy option in a Week 11 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday, irrespective of McConkey's availability.

With Ladd McConkey (back) sidelined, Harris functioned as a de facto top target for Justin Herbert, and he was responsible for all but 43 of his quarterback's passing yards. The yardage tally also was a career-high figure for Harris, who generated team-high totals with all three components of his receiving line. Harris is up to a career-high 348 receiving yards on 26 catches heading into a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday.

Herbert ironically compiled his second-fewest passing yards of the season in the Chargers' first victory, but the talented signal-caller leaned heavily on both his legs and an effective rushing performance from Omarion Hampton. Herbert made a significant contribution himself to cap off Los Angeles' opening drive of the game, taking off when he couldn't find anyone open and recording a 22-yard rushing touchdown for the first points of the night. The game also marked Herbert's first interception-free performance of the season and gives the beleaguered Chargers' air attack something to hang its collective hat on heading into a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday.

On the momentous occasion of the Chargers' long-awaited first win of the season, Hampton made a significant contribution with a season-high rushing yardage total. Shelley is dealing with an apparent ankle injury, and his status for the remainder of the second half is now uncertain. In his absence, Deane Leonard is a top candidate to see an increase in workload in the secondary with Los Angeles.

Thompson will not suit up for Monday's primetime clash after being listed as doubtful following a third consecutive DNP on Saturday, and it's no surprise the fourth-round rookie is unable to play in Monday's game. Derius Davis will take on the role of No. 4 wide receiver in the contest behind starters Quentin Johnston, Tre' Harris and KeAndre Lambert-Smith.
Awosika will suit up Monday for the first time since Week 2, when he suffered an injury to his fibula. He should slide back into his starting role at left guard.

Eboigbe suffered an ankle injury against the Texans in Week 9, and he will be sidelined for Monday night's contest. Nick Barrett should see an uptick in defensive snaps in the absence of Eboigbe, whose next chance to play is Week 11 against the Jets on Nov. 22.

Pipkins has been sidelined since Week 1, but he had his 21-day practice window opened Thursday and was listed as questionable heading into Monday. Assuming he can continue practicing in Week 11 without issue, Pipkins could be activated ahead of the Chargers' next game Nov. 22 versus the Jets. Once reinstated, Pipkins could settle back in as the team's starting left guard.
Taylor is battling an ankle injury and was ruled out for the Week 10 meeting with Baltimore. Now on injured reserve, he will be required to miss at least four games before being eligible to return.
Perryman is finally cleared to suit up after missing the entire season due to a pec issue. While his return is good news for the Chargers, it may take him a game or two to get back to full speed.

Nacua currently resides on injured reserve due to PCL and MCL sprains and a turf toe injury, for which he still must miss at least three games. Schefter's report also notes that the league communicated to the wideout that that any further violation of the personal conduct policy, including failing to satisfy the conditions of his diversion program, would subject him to additional and more substantial discipline, including banishment from the league.

Garrett was cleared to play in Week 10 after working through a knee injury. The low snap count was more due to the fact that the Cardinals posted only 35 offensive snaps while recording a 17:37 time of possession. The Rams are on a bye for Week 11, so Garrett's next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25.

Lake recorded at least six tackles in each of the first nine games of the regular season, but he had only two stops in Week 10 despite playing every defensive snap.
