Daniels' playing time isn't worth chasing in fantasy.

Despite both Puka Nacua (toe/knee) and Davante Adams (hamstring) being sidelined, Atwell still played just 16 of 76 offensive snaps versus Arizona and ran 15 routes on Matthew Stafford's 28 dropbacks. Atwell played behind both Konata Mumpfield and CJ Daniels at receiver for Los Angeles.

Amazingly, all 15 of Rivers' carries came on the Rams' final drive of the game, where they ran 17 plays to kill the final 12 minutes and 15 seconds of the clock. Rivers rushed 15 straight times before Matthew Stafford performed a pair of kneel-downs to end the game. It will be interesting to see if Rivers' efficiency was enough to earn him more carries before garbage time moving forward, especially after Kyren Williams looked stuck in the mud against Arizona, rushing 12 times for just 23 yards. For now, Rivers is simply a name to keep an eye on over the next couple of weeks, with the Rams wanting to lean on the run due to all of their high-profile pass-catching injuries.

With all three of Puka Nacua (knee/toe), Davante Adams (hamstring) and Terrance Ferguson (hamstring) out, the Rams leaned on their tight-end triumvirate of Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson and Allen, as all three played more offensive snaps than any of the Los Angeles wideouts. Parkinson (53 snaps) led the way, followed by Allen (52) and Higbee (51), and both Allen and Higbee caught touchdowns. Allen, however, ran just six routes on Matthew Stafford's 28 dropbacks, so it's not enough to warrant consideration in fantasy leagues.

McManus' Sunday performance extends his perfect streak with a Rams' special teams unit that desperately needed consistency at kicker. He's now 5-for-5 on field-goal attempts and 14-for-14 on PATs after five regular-season contests as a Ram in 2026.

Higbee's third and final catch of Sunday's game came late in the second quarter, with the veteran tight end connecting with Matthew Stafford for a five-yard touchdown to give the Rams a 10-6 lead. It was the second touchdown of the season for Higbee, with his first taking place in Week 3 against the Broncos. He's been held to three catches or fewer in each of his last four games, although he's been on the field for at least 50 offensive snaps in three of those contests. The Rams are on bye for Week 11, and Higbee's limited target share will take a hit if Davante Adams (hamstring) is activated from injured reserve ahead of Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25.

Parkinson was able to shed an injury designation for Sunday's game after having his practice reps limited during Week 10 prep due to a lingering rib injury. His second catch of the contest went for 10 yards early in the third quarter and set the Rams up on the 1-yard line, with Blake Corum finding the end zone on the next play. Parkinson was on the field for 53 of the Rams' 76 offensive snaps (69.7 percent), and fellow tight ends Davis Allen (52) and Tyler Higbee (51) were not far behind. The Rams are committed to using their 13-man personnel, although the game plan could be slightly tweaked after the Week 11 bye if wide receiver Davante Adams (hamstring) is activated from injured reserve ahead of Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25. Parkinson has caught 20 passes (on 25 targets) for 127 yards and a touchdown through eight regular-season games.

The starting center is set to miss 4-6 weeks with a hamstring injury. Shelton will likely be placed on injured reserve while he recovers. McMahon suffered a knee injury during the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday. With Coleman Shelton nursing a hamstring injury, the Rams may have to turn to other options like David Quessenberry or Beaux Limmer to fill in at center for the time being.

With the Rams down both Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring) for the first time this season, Smith operated as the fourth receiver against Arizona, playing nine of 76 offensive snaps. His 22-yard touchdown in the second quarter was the first of Smith's career. Based on his small amount of playing time and routes run, Smith's 12-point PPR day isn't worth chasing in fantasy.

With Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring) on injured reserve, Mumpfield operated as the de facto No. 1 receiver for Matthew Stafford. Mumpfield met the moment with a team-high receiving yardage total that more than doubled that of the next-closest pass catcher, Xavier Smith (40 yards). The 2025 seventh-round pick has now cleared the 80-yard mark twice this season, but Mumpfield could slide down to the No. 2 role in a Week 12 Thanksgiving Eve home matchup against the Packers on Nov. 25 if Adams is able to finish his recovery over the upcoming Week 11 bye.

Stafford didn't let the fact he was without top wideouts Puka Nacua (IR, knee/toe) and Davante Adams (IR, hamstring) deter him from a very fantasy-friendly performance, as the reigning NFL MVP tossed at least three TD passes for the fourth time this season. Stafford connected with the unlikely trio of Tyler Higbee (five yards), Xavier Smith (22 yards) and Davis Allen (19 yards) for his scoring strikes, and the quarterback's 9.6 yards per attempt was his second-highest figure of the season. Stafford, who'll have a chance to further build chemistry with his current wideouts during the Week 11 bye, could have Adams back for a Week 12 Thanksgiving Eve matchup against the Packers on Nov. 25, as reports earlier Sunday indicated the talented wideout is targeting that game for his return.

Williams was held well under 4.0 yards per carry for the third consecutive game, but Sunday's performance was particularly alarming in that he averaged a minuscule 1.9 yards per carry. In contrast, Blake Corum (17-100-1) and Ronnie Rivers (15-81-0, albeit in garbage time) both had multiple productive runs on the way to efficient afternoons, making Williams' struggles stand out all the more. With Corum particularly playing well in the last several weeks, Williams could be relegated to a clear complementary role in a Week 12 Thanksgiving Eve home showdown with the Packers on Nov. 25, following a Week 11 bye.

Corum was far more productive than backfield mate Kyren Williams, who he outpaced by five carries and 77 rushing yards. It was the fourth straight game with double-digit rush attempts and a touchdown for Corum, with Sunday's score coming from one yard out early in the third quarter. He has at least 73 rushing yards in three of the last four contests, and it remains to be seen if Sunday's division of labor will have any sticking power when Los Angeles returns to action following a Week 11 bye in a Week 12 home Thanksgiving Eve matchup against the Packers on Nov. 25.

McDuffie missed three of the Rams' last four games due to a persistent back injury. The cornerback is all set to suit up for Sunday's game, as he and Kam Curl return to reinforce the Rams' secondary in time for a divisional matchup with the Cardinals' rookie quarterback Carson Beck.

Douglas said earlier this week that he was planning to play Sunday, and head coach Jeff Hafley backed up that statement while speaking prior to Friday's practice. The Dolphins will reveal whether or not Douglas carries an injury designation into Sunday's contest at some point Friday afternoon.

Fellow defensive lineman Jordan Phillips (biceps) was also placed on IR on Tuesday, and as a result, Kenneth Grant will operate as the team's top dog at defensive tackle moving forward this season.

Wright was on the field for 12 of the Dolphins' 69 offensive snaps (17.4 percent), which was far behind lead back Ollie Gordon (49 snaps). Wright is averaging only 1.6 YPC on 25 rushes through seven regular-season games, and most of his on-field impact has come on special teams as a returner on kickoffs. The Dolphins will stay on the road for Week 11 against the Bills on Nov. 22.

Allen found the ball on both of his offensive snaps during Sunday's loss, although he ended up losing four yards on his only catch of the game early in the second quarter. He's well behind Ollie Gordon and Jaylen Wright on the running back depth chart, and most of Allen's playing time in Week 11 against the Bills on Nov. 22, likely will come on special teams.

Wilson has logged at least 0.5 sacks in three of his last four outings, and the veteran linebacker is up to 57 tackles (30 solo), including 4.0 sacks, and one pass defense through nine regular-season games.

Richter will now be forced to miss at least four games after suffering a foot injury during the Week 10 win over the Packers. The 26-year-old has compiled six tackles (three solo) across nine appearances this season while playing almost exclusively on special teams.

Van Ginkel sustained a quadriceps injury during the Vikings' 30-10 win over the Packers in Week 10. His ability to practice Wednesday indicates that the injury isn't a serious one, and an increase in participation over the coming days would put Van Ginkel on track to play in Sunday's road game against the 49ers in Mexico City.

Jones was elevated from the Vikings' practice squad to the active roster for both Week 5 and Week 10 against the Saints and Packers, respectively, and he'll now be part of Minnesota's 53-man roster moving forward. The addition of Jones to the active roster gives the Vikings extra depth at wide receiver in the absence of Jordan Addison (thumb).

Jennings sat out the last two games due to a calf injury, but his return to all activity Wednesday gives the Vikings' receiving corps a boost after Jordan Addison was lost for at least a few weeks due to a broken thumb that required surgery. All three of Reichard's field goals came from fewer than 40 yards out in the contest. The return of Kirk Cousins allowed Minnesota's offense to surge to its highest touchdown total since Week 1, the team's first bout against the Packers. Reichard is now 23-for-25 on field-goal attempts and remains perfect at 13-for-13 on PATs over nine regular-season games in 2026.

Price reeled in a season-high four passes for 49 yards and a score during Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers. The wideout was operating in a more prominent offensive role for the second week in a row with Jauan Jennings (calf) sidelined, and fellow wide receiver Jordan Addison (thumb) was unable to play as well. Addison now is expected to undergo thumb surgery, opening the door for Price to operate in an elevated position in Minnesota's offense for the time being.

Felton drew a start in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers, reeling in a season-high three of five targets for 33 yards over 56 offensive snaps. The wide receiver stepped into a starting role as a result of Jordan Addison (thumb) and Jauan Jennings (calf) being sidelined, and Addison is now reportedly set to undergo surgery to address his injury, opening the door for more opportunities for Felton moving forward.

Jordan Mason led the Vikings with 59 rushing yards, but Jones had the more productive afternoon as he scored his first TD since Week 5 on a one-yard plunge in the second quarter. Mason has yet to get into the end zone in four games since returning from a thumb injury, piecing together 182 rushing yards on 4.0 yards per carry while working in a timeshare with Jones. He could break that drought in Week 11 in a potential revenge game against the 49ers.

Brought back to Minnesota at the trade deadline to stabilize the offense, Cousins did exactly that, connecting with Myles Price for a 38-yard TD in the first quarter and Gavin Bartholomew on a 20-yard score in the fourth while guiding Justin Jefferson to season highs in catches and targets. Cousins may need to find another gear in Week 11 against the 49ers, but he'll have another week of practice to re-familiarize himself with Kevin O'Connell's scheme first.

In Kirk Cousins' return to the Vikings, Jefferson led the team in catches, targets and receiving yards, although Myles Price and Gavin Bartholomew were on the other end of the QB's two touchdown passes. Despite a disappointing 40-467-4 line on 64 targets through eight games, the star wideout's outlook for the rest of the year is pointed up heading into a Week 11 clash with the 49ers.

Metellus was added to the Vikings' practice report Friday due to a shoulder issue, but the injury won't prevent the seventh-year pro from suiting up for Sunday's NFC North showdown. He has 58 tackles (29 solo), including 0.5 sacks, and four pass defenses through eight regular-season games.

Kyler Murray (hamstring) is out for another week but may eventually replace Wentz as the No. 2 quarterback. Wentz's miserable performance against the Bills last week likely was a factor in the Vikings trading for Cousins.

Dallas notched just eight offensive snaps but also contributed 19 snaps on special teams. The whole Patriots' offense struggled after Drake Maye (ankle) was knocked out of the game early, but Stevenson also didn't look to be in peak form after dealing with a knee issue during the practice week. Corey Kiner wound up leading the backfield with just 25 rushing yards on 10 totes. Stevenson will get a Week 11 bye to rest up, and if Maye's injury ends up sidelining him for an extended period, New England could lean heavily on its running game in Week 12 against the Chargers.

Jones left the game during the fourth quarter, and given the score of the contest, the veteran linebacker is unlikely to return to Sunday's game. If that's the case, then Jones will finish with two tackles (one solo) and one QB hit.

Spillane went to the locker room in the third quarter, and he's being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return to Sunday's international game. Darius Muasau has taken over for Spillane at inside linebacker.

Moses went to the locker room in the first quarter to have his knee injury evaluated. He's been cleared by medical staff to return and is back in at right tackle, with backup Caleb Lomu now on the sidelines.

Van Roten will be available to make his season debut after spending the first nine weeks of the campaign on injured reserve due to the hamstring issue. He was able to practice throughout Week 10 prep, turning in a pair of a limited sessions Wednesday and Thursday before upgrading to full activity Friday, and the Patriots activated him Saturday. With Ben Brown (knee) and Walter Rouse (concussion) inactive for the Germany game, Van Roten will likely draw the start at left guard.

The biceps injury McCoy suffered back in Week 9 versus the Browns was expected to keep him out for multiple games, and he seems to be trending toward being out again in Week 11. If he can't return to practice Friday, Cesar Ruiz will likely be in line to start at center Sunday at Chicago, which would leave the starting right guard spot to rookie fourth-rounder Jeremiah Wright.

Fuaga is recovering from a knee strain he sustained a week ago, and his availability for Week 11 is in serious doubt. Unless he's somehow able to return to practice Friday, he'll probably end up on the sidelines during Sunday's game at Chicago.

The second-year quarterback suffered two broken bones in his left hand back on Oct. 5 and has been playing with the glove ever since. He's also been able to only hand the ball off with his right hand since suffering the injury. Shough has completed 66.8 percent of his passes for 2,173 yards, 15 touchdowns and seven interceptions across nine starts this season. He's averaging one full yard less per pass attempt (6.3) and 1.3 fewer yards per completion (9.5) compared to his 2025 rookie season.

Tyson maintained his activity level from Wednesday as he tends to a chest injury in the wake of his 11-80-0 line on 13 targets from the second game of his career this past Sunday versus the Panthers. Friday's practice report will determine if he has a designation ahead of Sunday's contest at Chicago.

Emerson entered the league's concussion protocol following the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers in Week 10, and he finished that contest with only one assisted tackle. He'll have two more chances to return to practice, but even if he does get some reps under his belt, he would need to be cleared of the league's protocol in order to play against the Bears on Sunday. Quincy Riley would likely start opposite Kool-Aid McKinstry if Emerson is sidelined for Week 11.

Werner suffered a hamstring injury in the first half of the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers in Week 10 and did not return. He'll have two more opportunities to practice in at least a limited capacity, but if he cannot play against the Bears on Sunday, then Danny Stutsman would be the top candidate to start alongside Kaden Elliss at inside linebacker.

Donaldson missed the Saints' last three games due to a shoulder injury, but his full practice Wednesday indicates that he'll be available for Sunday's road game against the Bears. Even if Donaldson does suit up, his role in the backfield figures to be minimal, seeing as Travis Etienne is off injured reserve and Alvin Kamara and Audric Estime are also available for the Saints.

Elliss was all over the field Sunday with a career-high 15 tackles (11 in the first half), which included an eight-yard sack on Bryce Young on the final play of the third quarter. Elliss has logged 10-plus tackles and a sack in back-to-back games, and the veteran linebacker is up to 56 stops (29 solo), including 2.0 sacks, and two pass defenses across six regular-season games.

The rookie fourth-rounder didn't see a target from Tyler Shough during Sunday's loss, and Lance has not recorded a catch in each of his last two outings, coinciding with the return of 2026 first-round wide receiver Jordyn Tyson. Lance's nine offensive snaps were a season low, and he figures to be limited to return duties now that Tyson is back in the fold. The Saints will hit the road for Week 11 against the Bears on Nov. 22.

Fant didn't connect with Tyler Shough on a short pass late in the first quarter, and that ended up being the only target for the veteran tight end. Fant has a 12-96-3 line on 19 targets through eight regular-season games, although he's logged one reception or zero in four of his last five outings. He doesn't have much fantasy appeal as the Saints' TE2 behind Juwan Johnson heading into Week 11 against the Bears on Nov. 22.

Vele was on the field for 55 of the Saints' 63 offensive snaps, which was second most among wide receivers behind Chris Olave (56). Despite that playing time, Vele saw only two targets Sunday, although no other Saints pass catcher logged more than three receptions other than rookie first-rounder Jordyn Tyson, who finished with 11 catches on 13 targets for 80 yards. Vele has two receptions in each of his last two outings, and it appears his role in the Saints' passing offense has shrunk due to the return of Tyson. Vele will look to bounce back for Week 11 against the Bears on Nov. 22, and Chicago's defense ranks 15th in the NFL in fantasy points allowed to receivers per game.

For a second week in a row, Smyth operated as the Saints' kicker during the team's 20-17 loss to the Panthers on Sunday, when he made both of his extra-point tries and connected on a 55-yard field goal late in the fourth quarter. Daniel Carlson was released by New Orleans on Nov. 3, so Smyth likely will be elevated to the active roster for Week 11 against the Bears on Nov. 22.

Richards injured his knee during the fourth quarter of Sunday's game and wasn't cleared by medical staff to return. The injury appears severe enough for him to warrant an extended period of time on the shelf, so Richards is a candidate to be placed on injured reserve. Mason Murphy will likely move into the starting spot at right tackle for as long as Richards is sidelined.

With Jordyn Tyson playing his second game since debuting last week, the rookie wideout was targeted 13 times on Tyler Shough's 35 pass attempts. It didn't leave much for the rest of New Orleans' pass catchers, as Travis Etienne was actually second on the team with five targets. Over his last five games, Johnson has nine catches for 85 yards and a score. He's become a low-end TE2 for fantasy.

Travis Etienne returned from IR and led the Saints' backfield with 11 touches, although he managed just 34 scrimmage yards, while Alvin Kamara handled five touches and scored two short TDs. Perhaps worse for Estime's role and future value, he was ineffective in short-yardage situations, getting stuffed on three attempts to pick up a first down from two yards out or less, and a miscommunication with Tyler Shough on a handoff led to a lost fumble in the second quarter, although the giveaway was charged to the QB. Estime will try to maintain some share of the workload in a Week 11 meeting with the Bears.

Seeing his first action since Week 3 after recovering from a hamstring strain, the former Jaguar led the Saints' backfield with 11 touches, ahead of Audric Estime's eight and Alvin Kamara's five. Etienne wasn't able to do much with the volume, however, while Kamara scored two short TDs. Etienne still appears to be the top option for the team at RB, but if Estime keeps taking short-yardage work and Kamara is the preferred red-zone back, it would put a real ceiling on Etienne's upside. He'll look to claim a bigger share of the workload in Week 11 against the Bears.

The game wound up being Jordyn Tyson's breakout performance, as the rookie WR hauled in 11 of 13 targets for 80 yards, but that didn't leave much volume for Olave or any other Saint. With Tyler Shough struggling, it's unclear whether the passing game can keep more than one pass catcher fantasy-relevant at a time. Olave sports a 59-774-2 line on 87 targets through nine games, and he'll look to bounce back in a Week 11 tilt against the Bears.

With Travis Etienne back from his weeks-long hamstring injury that saw him miss five games while on injured reserve, the Saints deployed a three-man backfield committee against Carolina. Kamara scored a couple touchdowns, but it was a fluky performance on just five touches and 16 offensive snaps. Audric Estime logged 27 snaps and handled eight touches, while Etienne played 21 snaps and touched the ball 11 times. This is a backfield to avoid in fantasy while it the trio cancels each other out and caps each others' upside.

Miller is dealing with a knee injury and is now required to miss at least four games. The rookie nose tackle has played in four games this season, logging five tackles (two solo) over 93 snaps on defense and four snaps on special teams. Nathan Shepherd and Khristian Boyd could both get more defensive snaps during Miller's absence.

Edwards' practice reps were limited Wednesday and Thursday due to a knee injury, but he avoided an injury tag for Week 10 after logging a full session Friday. He has started in each of the Saints' first eight games of the regular season.

Banks was able to avoid an injury tag after logging a full practice Friday. Sunday's game will be his second since being activated from injured reserve Nov. 7 due to a high-ankle sprain that he suffered in Week 2 against the Ravens.

Harrison missed the Giants' contest versus the Commanders in Week 10 because of a groin injury, but it appears he'll be able to return to game action in Week 11. Of his 141 total snaps so far in 2026, 136 have come on special teams.

Pinnock left the Giants' game versus the Commanders in Week 10 with a back injury after just 15 defensive snaps, but it looks like he's back to full strength for Week 11. He should play a rotational role in the Giants' secondary during Sunday's contest against a run-heavy Jacksonville offense.

The Giants haven't provided any updates on Tracy since he landed on IR on Oct. 27 after sustaining a hamstring strain in a Week 7 win over the Texans, but the running back is seemingly progressing well and could be ready to play once he sits out the required four games. Once he's reinstated, Tracy could operate as a change-of-pace option behind Cam Skattebo, who appears to have reclaimed the lead role out of the New York backfield after a one-game benching in Week 6.

J.J. McCarthy made his third consecutive start for the Giants, but Winston continued to get sprinkled into the game plan during short-yardage situations. He extended a second-quarter drive that culminated in a Cam Skattebo touchdown by gaining a yard on a fourth-and-one play, but Winston was dropped for no gain on a third-and-one run in the fourth quarter that resulted in a Giants punt. The Giants may continue to turn to Winston for quarterback sneaks in future weeks in an effort to limit the wear and tear on McCarthy.

Gipson will head to New York after spending the entirety of the 2026 campaign to this point on the Eagles' practice squad. The Giants waived primary kick and punt returner Charlie Jones on Monday, and Gipson will likely take over that role beginning in Week 11 against the Jaguars.
McFadden logged one tackle for loss in the contest. The starting inside linebacker assisted the Giants in holding the Commanders to 3.2 yards per carry and no rushing touchdowns in the game.

Holland picked off Jayden Daniels with 2:19 left in the fourth quarter, just one Commanders drive after Ar'Darius Washington picked the quarterback off. Despite back-to-back turnovers, the Giants' offense logged back-to-back three-and-outs to put the Commanders' offense in position to win the game.

Washington broke up two passes in the contest, picking off Jayden Daniels with 5:31 left in the fourth quarter of Thursday's game. Despite making a crucial play with the Giants up four points, the offense could not put more points on the board to cement a primetime win.

Reese led the Giants in tackles as a consistent force against the Commanders' run game in the NFC East showdown. Despite the rookie first-rounder's best efforts, the Giants allowed 24 points en route to a meaningful divisional loss.

Zvada's miss was a chip-shot 33-yarder in the first quarter that sailed wide left. That proved to be a critical mistake, as the Commanders won by just three points. Zvada appeared to shore up his job security a bit by going 4-for-4 on FG tries in Week 9 against Philadelphia, but it's hard to ignore the fact that he's gone just 17-for-23 on field-goal attempts overall and has missed three kicks from under 50 yards. The rookie does have a perfect 16-for-16 mark on extra-point attempts, and head coach John Harbaugh expressed support for the inconsistent kicker Friday, saying of Zvada, "I'm confident that he's going to become a good kicker. If at some point and time it doesn't happen, it doesn't happen. But I'm not going to panic halfway through the season with a guy who has made a bunch of kicks," Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.

Johnson hasn't been able to get going in 2026, as he's finished with one or zero catches in six of his seven games so far. After working as New York's top tight end last season, he's been mostly an afterthought in the current campaign due to the arrival of Isaiah Likely, who went off for a 9-127-1 line on a team-leading 11 targets Thursday. As long as Likely is healthy, Johnson won't have much appeal in most fantasy formats.

Mooney logged the third-most targets of any New York pass catcher, but he managed just two short receptions. Efficiency has been an issue for the veteran wideout throughout the campaign, as he's hauled in only 14 of 30 targets through nine contests. Mooney has finished with fewer than 10 yards in four of his past six appearances, so he's not a viable fantasy play at the moment.

Cam Skattebo came back from a hamstring injury and dominated backfield work, taking 21 touches for 122 yards and two touchdowns on an 88 percent snap share. Singletary played 92 percent of snaps the week before in a win at Philadelphia, but his 23 touches went for just 39 total yards and no TDs. It'll likely be another large workload for Skattebo when the Giants host the Jaguars in Week 11.

The rookie finished a distant second in receiving yards to Isaiah Likely for the Giants on the night, but Fields' yardage total was the second highest of his nascent career. Fields has at least three catches in three consecutive games after opening his career with six straight two-reception efforts, and the Notre Dame product will look to continue cultivating his chemistry with J.J. McCarthy in a Week 11 home matchup against the Jaguars on Sunday, Nov. 22.

McCarthy continued to look like a competent NFL signal-caller in his third start for the Giants, posting a new career high in passing yards and adding a new season high in rushing yardage. His one touchdown pass was a critical one, as he hit Isaiah Likely over the middle for a 66-yard score just before the midway point of the fourth quarter to erase a 17-14 deficit. McCarthy has displayed excellent chemistry with his top targets, and he'll look to keep his hot streak going against a pass-funnel Jaguars defense in a Week 11 home matchup on Sunday, Nov. 22.

The star wideout finished with less than 50 receiving yards for the second time in five days, and Nabers' late third-quarter lost fumble had significant ramifications. The turnover came at the Commanders' 16-yard line with the Giants down by three, costing  New York a golden opportunity to tie the game at minimum. Nabers' aforementioned pair of mediocre performances have come in the wake of a four-game streak of 100-yard efforts in Weeks 4-7, and he'll look to boost his numbers back up against the Jaguars' pass-funnel defense in a Week 11 home matchup on Sunday, Nov. 22.

Likely set the pace for the Giants across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and his figure in the middle category also was a career high. The veteran tight end now has five double-digit target tallies on the campaign, and Thursday's production, which included a 66-yard catch-and-run touchdown in the third quarter, pushed his season line to a robust 55-575-7 line across nine games. All three components already are career-high figures, affording Likely massive momentum heading into a Week 11 home showdown against the Jaguars on Sunday, Nov. 22.

Skattebo put together an impressive all-around performance that included a season high in receiving yards. He also exceeded the 75-yard mark on the ground for the third time on the campaign, and he went in for his third and fourth rushing touchdowns of the season on one- and 13-yard runs in the first and third quarters, respectively. Skattebo didn't show any ill effects from the hamstring injury that cost him Sunday's win over the Eagles, and he'll now gear up for a Week 11 home matchup against the Jaguars' elite run defense on Sunday, Nov. 22.

With Omar Cooper (ankle/hip) also slated to be unavailable for the contest, Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell will lead the Jets' Week 11 WR corps, with coach Aaron Glenn noting Friday that the team's tight ends, primarily Kenyon Sadiq and Mason Taylor, should have an opportunity to see added opportunities as pass catchers this weekend in the absence of both Cooper and Williams.

While the initial report indicated only that Smith would practice, Eric Allen of the Jets' official website reported that Smith will be a full participant Friday, which makes it even more likely that he will be under center in Week 11. The Jets' final injury report will reveal whether or not Smith carries an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Chargers.

Cooper didn't practice Wednesday or Thursday due to a pair of injuries, and he'll wind up sitting out Week 11. Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell will be the primary wideouts for the Jets, and with Isaiah Williams (ribs) joining Cooper on the sidelines, Malik McClain and Tim Patrick will be options when the team wants to get more receivers on the field, and per head coach Aaron Glenn -- via Rich Cimini of ESPN.com -- Sterling Shepard and tight ends Kenyon Sadiq and Mason Taylor could also get involved.

The defensive tackle missed Wednesday's session. Phillips played on 53 percent of the Jets' defensive snaps in Sunday's loss to the Bills and hasn't missed a game this season. Now that he's back at practice, he looks like he has a good chance to play in Week 11 against the Chargers as well.

An illness prevented Brownlee from playing in the Jets' Week 10 loss to the Bills. His full practice Wednesday indicates that he is fully healthy and should be available for Sunday's road game against the Chargers.

Onyemata's 21-day practice window has been opened. The 34-year-old hasn't played since Week 2 against Green Bay, when he suffered a groin injury. Darrell Jackson, Jowon Briggs and Harrison Phillips have taken most snaps at defensive tackle in his absence.
Belton tied for third on the Jets with six stops. That's a total he's now reached in every game this season except Week 1. Belton ranks second among NFL safeties with 82 tackles on the campaign.

Davis' six tackles tied for third-most on the Jets. The veteran linebacker has been relatively consistent this season with between six and 10 stops in seven of his 10 games so far. Davis has 68 total tackles (including 2.0 sacks) through 10 games, putting him on pace for a 10th consecutive triple-digit tackle campaign.

Sherwood finished second on the Jets in stops Sunday, behind Harrison Phillips (10). Sherwood has notched at least eight tackles in five straight games, and he's hit the double-digit mark three times this season. The veteran linebacker ranks eighth in the NFL with 86 tackles through 10 games.

Sanders knocked in field goals from 41, 27, 22 and 48 yards out in Sunday's contest. The kicker accounted for all 12 of the Jets' points for a second straight week, performing the same feat in the team's Week 9 loss to the Chiefs. Sanders moves to 25-for-28 on field-goal attempts over nine contests so far during the 2026 season.

Taylor's four catches were tied with Breece Hall and Isaiah Williams for second most on the Jets behind Garrett Wilson, who turned 14 targets into a 7-106-1 line. It was the third time this season that Taylor recorded at least four catches, with his last instance being Week 7 against the Dolphins (five receptions). The second-year tight end has a 22-167-2 line on 29 targets through eight regular-season games heading into Week 11 against the Chargers on Nov. 22.

With Breece Hall and Braelon Allen both healthy, Davis has minimal fantasy value, except for leagues that count return yardage. He's played zero offensive snaps over the last two contests, but Davis did return three kickoffs for 74 yards against Buffalo.

Parham sustained the injury in the second quarter of Sunday's game and was not cleared to return. The Jets face the Chargers in Week 11 on Sunday, and if Parham cannot play in that contest, then Jordan Meredith would be the top candidate to fill in at left guard.

On a day in which quarterbacks Geno Smith (ankle) and Cade Klubnik dropped back 45 times, Sadiq wasn't able to see much involvement in the passing game. Though the rookie first-round pick put his pass-catching chops on display with a 7-105-1 receiving line in Week 3 against Detroit, he's since delivered a collective 10-95-0 line on 19 targets over the Jets' ensuing seven contests. A lack of extended playing time has been a factor in Sadiq's listless production of late; he's logged fewer than 50 percent of the offensive snaps in five of those seven games while second-year tight end Mason Taylor typically has handled larger snap shares.

With Garrett Wilson back from his one-game absence Sunday, Mitchell was left fighting for secondary looks. His eight targets were second on the team, trailing Wilson's 14, and Omar Cooper's early-game ankle injury helped Mitchell's volume solidify. If Cooper is going to miss time going forward, Mitchell will be a more comfortable fantasy WR3 play with upside headed into next Sunday's game against the Chargers.

For a second consecutive game, Allen was outplayed by Breece Hall, who produced 108 scrimmage yards on 15 touches. Allen remains the more efficient runner, averaging 5.0 yards per carry to Hall's 3.4 this season, but Hall is the team's preferred option in passing situations, which have been plentiful with the 2-8 Jets frequently in catch-up mode. Perhaps a Week 11 matchup with a Chargers team that's still searching for its first win through Sunday of Week 10 will offer an opportunity to stick with the run and play to Allen's strengths.

Klubnik saw the first regular-season action of his NFL career in the second half of Sunday's loss, as Geno Smith (ankle) exited the game. The rookie fourth-round pick led the offense down to Buffalo's four-yard line on his first possession in the third quarter, but the Jets settled for a field goal on that possession, and Klubnik was picked off on his next drive. If Smith isn't ready to return in Week 11, Klubnik would be in line to make his first regular-season start on the road against the Chargers.

Hall narrowly topped Braelon Allen (eight carries for 40 yards) for the team lead in rushing yards and finished second behind Garrett Wilson (seven catches for 106 yards) in both receptions and receiving yards. While Allen continues to be more efficient as a rusher, Hall's superior receiving ability should help the latter maintain the edge in playing time for a 2-8 Jets team that often finds itself playing catch-up. Rookie QB Cade Klubnik, who played most of the second half Sunday, could be more reliant on check downs to Hall than veteran Geno Smith (ankle) was, but it remains to be seen who will get the nod under center in Week 11 against the Chargers.

Wilson set a new season high in targets and came one yard short of his Week 3 season high Sunday in his return from a one-game absence due to a concussion. His production came on a mix of passes from Geno Smith (ankle) and rookie Cade Klubnik, the latter of whom saw his first NFL action after Smith exited in the second half. Wilson figures to work as the top target for whomever starts under center in a Week 11 road game against the Chargers.

Payne missed the Jets' first nine games of the regular season while on injured reserve due to a bone bruise in his knee. He was activated from IR on Saturday, and the rookie seventh-rounder was given the green light to make his NFL regular-season debut in Week 10.

Shipley is still on injured reserve but had his 21-day practice window opened this week. With Saquon Barkley healthy right now, Shipley has minimal fantasy appeal in a broken Philadelphia offense that is near the bottom of the league in most categories over the last month.

Wicks is seeking his first game action since Week 6 due to an ankle injury, and he still has some work to do after kicking off Week 11 prep with back-to-back capped sessions. Friday's practice report will reveal his odds to play Sunday versus the Steelers.

Smith followed up Wednesday's limited showing with an uncapped session one day later, thereby paving the way for his first game action since Week 6. Despite missing five of the last six contests due to a hamstring injury, he put together a 26-310-2 line on 41 targets in his four appearances this season. However, with Jalen Hurts (blood clots) out for the rest of the 2026 campaign, Smith will be on the receiving end of passes from Joe Milton on Sunday against the Steelers.

Smith's practice reps were capped during Wednesday's session due to an illness. The fourth-year pro will have two more opportunities to log a full practice and avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against Pittsburgh. Smith has 17 tackles (nine solo), including 5.0 sacks, and one pass defense across eight regular-season games.

Campbell was sidelined for each of the Eagles' two contests prior to the Week 10 bye due to hamstring and quadriceps injuries. The second-year linebacker made the most of the extra rest courtesy of the bye, and he is on track to return against the Steelers on Sunday.

Baun injured his back during the Eagles' Week 9 loss to the Giants. He's had additional time to rest due to the Week 10 bye, but he was not cleared to practice Wednesday. He'll have two more opportunities to return to practice in at least a limited capacity ahead of Sunday's game against the Steelers.

Though the Eagles dropped a seventh straight game while Milton turned the ball over once and took seven sacks in a Week 9 loss to the Giants, Sirianni saw enough from the third-year signal-caller to hand him at least one more start. While it's conceivable that the Eagles could go back to McKee -- who started Weeks 6 through 8 -- at some point if Milton's performance isn't up to par, rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton is also on the roster and may get a look before the season winds down.

While starting in his team debut Week 9 against the Giants, Milton was unable to bring an end to the Eagles' lengthy losing streak, but the third-year quarterback showed enough positives to retain the starting gig coming out of a Week 10 bye. Milton put an intriguing dual-threat skill set on display with 64 yards on nine carries to go with 169 passing yards on 34 attempts in the 19-11 loss to New York, with the rushing output in particular perhaps making him worth a look in superflex leagues or leagues that start two quarterbacks. He lost a fumble and took seven sacks in the loss to the Giants, so Milton may need to show that he can avoid negative plays in Week 11 in order to guarantee himself additional starts.

It's already the third time this season Blue has been signed by Philadelphia from the practice squad to the active roster. The second-year pro has seen action in two games with the club, recording a nine-yard catch on his only touch while racking up 268 yards on 12 kickoff returns. Blue is currently the only healthy running back on the Eagles' active roster aside from starter Saquon Barkley, but that may change soon, as Will Shipley (foot - IR) had his practice window opened Monday. Elijah Mitchell has been promoted from the practice squad to help in the backfield each of the past three weeks, so he'd need to be signed to the active roster as well in order to suit up against Pittsburgh this Sunday.

Philadelphia is coming off a Week 10 bye, but prior to the midseason respite, there were no reported injuries in the TE group on the active roster. When the position group was depleted earlier this season, the team used elevations on Ertz from Weeks 3-5, but his snap share decreased game by game (38, 21 and 11 percent), while he hauled in three of eight targets for 22 yards in that span. Wednesday's practice report will reveal if any of Dallas Goedert, Eli Stowers, Johnny Mundt or Grant Calcaterra are banged up at the moment.

Trotter was on the field for 64 of the Eagles' 67 defensive snaps (95.5 percent), and he was the only Philadelphia defender to reach double-digit stops. He's tallied at least 10 tackles three times in 2026, and the third-year pro is up to 51 tackles (32 solo), including 0.5 sacks, one pass defense and one forced fumble through nine regular-season games.

Week 9 was the Eagles' first game with Joe Milton as the starter, with Tanner McKee relegated to backup duties. Milton completed 18 of his 34 passes, and his lone connection with Moore resulted in a three-yard loss. The Eagles are on a bye for Week 10, and Moore's role on the offense would evaporate if one or both of DeVonta Smith (hamstring) or Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) was cleared to play in Week 11 against the Steelers on Sunday, Nov. 22.

With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) still out, Cooper played more than 90 percent of the offensive snaps for the third straight game. He's done very little with that playing time, producing five catches for 61 yards during that span. Cooper is well off the fantasy radar until he shows something in the box score, and that's if Smith and Wicks remain sidelined.

Earlier Tuesday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network relayed that the Eagles agreed to send Ebiketie to the Bengals in exchange for a 2027 sixth-round pick. The trade wasn't cancelled due to concerns over Ebiketie's physical; instead, the Bengals opted to call it off since they would have lost a third-round compensatory pick if the deal was completed, per Rapoport. The Eagles could still look to move Ebiketie elsewhere prior to Tuesday's deadline, but barring another trade, he'll suit up for Philadelphia in its Week 10 game against Pittsburgh.

Mitchell has been elevated each of the past three weeks and has logged at least six touches in every game during that span. During this past Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants, he recorded six yards on three carries and caught three passes for 20 yards on four targets. The Eagles would need to sign Mitchell to the 53-man roster in order for him to be eligible to play in their next game, which will be Nov. 22 versus Pittsburgh following a Week 10 bye. That opportunity for Mitchell could depend on whether Tank Bigsby (abdomen) and/or Will Shipley (foot) return from injured reserve.

Elliott's kick was good from 45 yards, but with Joe Milton making his first start at quarterback and without DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), the Philly offense struggled to move the ball and score points. Elliott is not an exciting fantasy kicker on a tanking Eagles team.

The rookie tight end ran just four routes on Joe Milton's 48 dropbacks against the G-Men. Grant Calcaterra ran just six, as the Eagles used more three-wide sets than multiple TE sets. Stowers would need a Dallas Goedert injury or trade to come into any fantasy value.

Lemon showed a nice rapport with QB Joe Milton in Milton's first NFL start, as the rookie first-round pick led the Eagles in catches, receiving yards and targets. Lemon has operated as Philadelphia's de facto No. 1 WR while DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) have both missed the past three games, but the Eagles could get at least one of their top two wideouts back in Week 11 against the Steelers following a Week 10 bye.

Goedert finished one catch and 11 yards shy of Makai Lemon's team-leading totals in Joe Milton's first start for the Eagles. Both of Goedert's touchdowns this season came back in Week 1, and the Eagles have since changed QBs twice. Goedert's best result in the three games started by Tanner McKee was a six-catch, 61-yard outing, so the veteran TE has remained consistent even as the offense around him falls apart due to injuries. Milton, McKee and rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton are all potential candidates to start in Week 11 against the Steelers after Philadelphia's Week 10 bye.

Barkley has mustered a meager 2.0 yards per carry over the past two games while playing through hamstring and back injuries, but he also has both of Philadelphia's touchdowns over that span, including a three-yard rushing score in the second quarter Sunday. It has been a slog offensively for the Eagles, who have tried first Tanner McKee and now Joe Milton under center since losing starting QB Jalen Hurts (IR, calf) likely for the season while also playing without top two wide receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). It's fair to wonder if Barkley will eventually be shut down as well to get a chance to heal as the 2-7 Eagles drop out of contention, but at least a Week 10 bye will offer him a respite before Philadelphia's Week 11 home game against the Steelers.

The safety had to sit out of the Steelers' Week 10 loss to the Bengals after injuring his knee during pregame warmups, but he was able to return to practice on a limited basis Wednesday. Now that he's upgraded to full participation, he looks good to go for Sunday's matchup with the Eagles. Elliott has logged two solo tackles across 43 defensive snaps and five special-teams snaps in two games this season.

With a second full practice under his belt since being designated for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Wilson looks poised to get activated ahead of Sunday's game against the Eagles. Prior to missing time with a dislocated finger and a fractured digit on his left hand, Wilson had averaged five targets per game over his five appearances, but he could struggle to see that level of volume upon returning. Fellow wideout Michael Pittman (foot) was also a full participant in Thursday's practice and could be a candidate to return from IR this week, and rookie second-round pick Germie Bernard may have performed well enough over the last handful of games to retain a notable role in the Steelers' receiving corps.

After being designated for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Pittman was able to return to a limited practice. The WR's presence at Thursday's session implies that there were no setbacks, with the Steelers' upcoming injury report set to reveal his official participation level. In any case, Pittman will need to be activated off IR no later than Saturday afternoon in order to have a chance to play Sunday against the Eagles.

Herbig likely suffered his hip injury in the Steelers' Week 10 loss to the Bengals. The reserve linebacker will likely need to upgrade to a full participant by Friday's practice to avoid any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Eagles.

Dunker went to IR with a sprained MCL back in late September, but it now looks like he's close to being available again. The move opens a 21-day window during which Pittsburgh can officially activate him before he'd have to go back on the shelf for the remainder of the campaign.

McCormick dislocated his ankle during the Steelers' 38-18 loss to the Bengals on Sunday. The good news for the third-year pro is that he avoided a fracture and does not require surgery, so there's a chance he could return for the Steelers should the team qualify for the playoffs, per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network. Brock Hoffman figures to start at left guard in McCormick's stead.

Queen may have picked up the injury during the Steelers' 38-18 loss to the Bengals in Week 10, when he logged 14 tackles (five solo), including 1.0 sacks. The veteran edge rusher will have two more chances to increase his practice participation and avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's road game against the Eagles. Queen has recorded double-digit tackles in each of his last three outings and has amassed 3.5 sacks in that span.

Pittsburgh gave up 38 points, so it wasn't exactly a stellar performance by the team's defense. However, three different Steelers players logged double-digit tackles -- including Brisker, who finished with 10. That's a season-high mark for the veteran safety, who has finished with at least six stops in all but one of his nine games so far this season.

Wilson not only set a career high with his 19 stops, he also tied the NFL high mark by any player so far this season. The third-year linebacker has jumped up a notch as an IDP asset in 2026, as he's tied for sixth in the league with 88 stops through nine games. Wilson has also added a sack, three defensed passes (including one interception) and a fumble recovery.

Boswell had an uneventful night, making his 45-yard field goal in the second quarter of the contest. The kicker moves to 19-for-24 on field-goal attempts and 17-for-17 on PATs over nine regular-season games in 2026.

Bernard went without a catch for the first time since Week 1, and his three targets were his fewest since the team's Week 4 loss to the Browns. The wide receiver led his position in offensive snaps (58), besting DK Metcalf (50) in that regard. Bernard entered Week 10 having recorded multiple receptions in five straight contests, and he'll have a good shot to get back on track in Week 11 versus the Eagles.

Aaron Rodgers threw for 143 yards in the game, and most of that came in garbage time in the second half with the score already out of hand. Washington has fewer than 30 receiving yards in seven of nine games played this season and is the epitome of a touchdown-or-bust fantasy option at tight end.

After the Bengals had built a 20-point lead with five minutes remaining in the fourth quarter, head coach Mike McCarthy opted to remove starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers from the game and turned to Rudolph to direct the offense for the Steelers' final possession. Rudolph led the Steelers on an 11-play drive that concluded in the red zone before time expired. The 31-year-old Rudolph has now made four relief appearances behind Rodgers on the season, playing limited snaps in each of those contests.

Metcalf's yardage total, modest as it was, led the Steelers on the night. The veteran receiver got there with the help of a team-long 32-yard catch, while his other reception was a 22-yard scoring grab early in the fourth quarter that Metcalf followed up with a two-point conversion. Metcalf has at least Sunday night's yardage total in three of the last four games, but he's still sporting an inefficient 35-432-2 line on 70 targets through nine games heading into a Week 11 road matchup against the Eagles next Sunday.

The Steelers were quickly dissuaded from a balanced offensive approach when the Bengals accumulated 24 first-half points, leading to Warren's lowest carry and rushing yardage totals of the season. Warren did tie his second-highest reception total of the campaign thanks in part to how the game unfolded, but it was ultimately a nearly irrelevant fantasy night relative to the lofty standards the versatile back has set this season. Warren will look to get back on track at the expense of the struggling Eagles in a Week 11 intrastate road showdown next Sunday.

Dowdle's previous low-water mark in touches was nine in Week 2 at New England, and on the season he averaged 11.8 touches per game entering Week 10 action. As a result, he finished with his second-fewest yards from scrimmage (34) in a contest this season, while backfield mate Jaylen Warren (12 touches for 41 total yards) also found little success in any facet. Dowdle remains the No. 2 RB in Pittsburgh behind Warren and thus is a hit-or-miss option in a Week 11 road matchup with the Eagles next Sunday.

Freiermuth was added to the Steelers' injury report Saturday due to an illness that left him questionable for Week 10 action. Ultimately, he avoided inactive status and also made an end-zone visit for the first time since Week 5 on a 27-yard hookup with QB Aaron Rodgers in the fourth quarter. Considering Freiermuth hasn't reached 50 receiving yards in any game this season, he remains a TD-dependent fantasy option (five in his nine appearances).

The Steelers sat at 33 total yards of offense after three quarters, so the vast majority of Rodgers' output occurred on the team's three fourth-quarter possessions, two of which ended in touchdown connections with WR DK Metcalf (22 yards) and TE Pat Freiermuth (27 yards). Through nine games this season, Rodgers has tossed multiple TDs on five occasions, but he's also been held to less than 200 yards through the air three times. Rodgers will seek better results next Sunday in Phildadelphia.

Howard has regularly worked in the emergency third-quarterback role this season, though it has yet to result in any game action. He'll be eligible to enter the matchup Sunday night only if both Aaron Rodgers and Mason Rudolph exit due to injury, illness or ejection.

Harmon landed on IR in early October due to a foot injury. He was designated to return this past Wednesday and logged an LP/LP/FP practice progression this week. Harmon is now set to return to the field Sunday night, though it's unclear if he'll be eased back into action in terms of defensive snap share.

Echols missed the last two games before Pittsburgh's bye in Week 9 because of a hamstring injury, but it looks like he's on track to be available in Week 10. Through six games so far in 2026, a substantial majority of his snaps have come on special teams.

Slaughter was unable to play against the Browns in Week 8 due to a hamstring injury that prevented him from practicing. His ability to log a full session Wednesday puts him on track to play against the Bengals on Sunday, when he's expected to play mostly on special teams while providing the Steelers depth in the secondary.

Green was not able to finish the 49ers' contest against the Cowboys in Week 10 because of his back injury, but it now seems like he's back to 100 percent. He projects to play a significant role in San Francisco's secondary during Sunday's game against Minnesota.

Greenlaw appeared on the 49ers' injury report with a neck issue Wednesday, but he took a step in the right direction Thursday with a limited practice session. If he can upgrade again Friday to a full practice, he may be able to avoid taking an injury designation into the weekend.

Jones popped up on the 49ers' injury report with an unspecified illness Wednesday, and now his status for Week 11 is up in the air. If he can't practice in full Friday, there's a decent chance he'll end up carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

Guerendo has been on the PUP list with a pec injury since training camp, but it now looks like he may be making some progress toward returning to action. Even if he does get back to full strength at some point soon, though, it's not clear how much room there will be for him in a 49ers' backfield that has recently been dominated by veteran Christian McCaffrey and rookie third-rounder Kaelon Black.
questionable

Head coach Kyle Shanahan and GM John Lynch both expressed hope that Evans would return to practice Thursday, and he indeed did enough to receive a limited listing. Evans is aiming for his first game action since a Week 6 win against the Commanders, when he aggravated a right Achilles injury. Friday's practice report will determine if Evans has a chance to play in Sunday's contest against the Vikings in Mexico City.

After he had missed the 49ers' first six games of the season while recovering from a calf injury, Kirk landed on injured reserve for the second time this season back on Nov. 7 due to a right knee injury sustained in his team debut Week 7 in Atlanta. Since Kirk didn't specify whether he required a partial meniscectomy or a meniscus repair, his exact recovery timeline isn't known. Regardless, he'll have to miss at least two more games while he's on IR.

Brown likely suffered his ankle injury in the 49ers' Week 10 win over the Cowboys. The free safety played 74 percent of the team's defensive snaps in the contest. Brown will likely need to upgrade to a full practice participant by Friday to avoid any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Vikings.
questionable

questionable

This is the first time Stribling has participated in on-field work since suffering a significant ankle injury in the Week 1 win over the Rams. The expectation has been that the rookie could be back by December, so Stribling is progressing toward hitting that goal. Once Stribling progresses to full-team drills, his timeline will get more dialed in. The 49ers have two more games in November, leaving the Week 13 matchup against the Giants as his earliest potential return date.

After Aiyuk filed his paperwork for reinstatement, San Francisco activated him from the reserve/left squad list Nov. 9. Rosenhaus noted that Aiyuk passed his physical at that time, with MRIs and X-rays on his surgically repaired knee revealing no concerns. The 49ers were granted a two-week roster exemption for Aiyuk that will expire next Monday, and the 28-year-old wideout is expected to be cut loose at that time since San Francisco seemingly hasn't expressed interested in retaining him. While it's unclear what kind of market might exist for Aiyuk's services coming off a lengthy layoff from NFL action, NFL reporter Jordan Schultz relayed earlier this month that at least one NFC team has expressed interest in adding the receiver to its practice squad.

Warner had a strong outing in the victory, leading the team in tackles while playing all 83 defensive snaps. The 29-year-old has now compiled 88 tackles (38 solo), including 0.5 sacks, five forced fumbles and a fumble recovery across nine games this season.

Cowing was also sent back to receive two punts in Week 10, making a fair catch on one and allowing the other to go into the endzone for a touchback. He has now drawn just one target over the two games following his three-catch performance in Week 7, and his role in the 49ers' offense figures to shrink even further once veteran Mike Evans returns from Achilles tendinitis, which could happen as soon as Sunday versus Minnesota.

Robinson's snap count was fourth-most among San Francisco's wide receivers, but his role in the offense shrunk due to the return of Deebo Samuel and the acquisition of Keenan Allen at the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Brandin Cooks (coach's decision) was a healthy scratch for Week 10, and Robinson could join the former on the sidelines for Week 11 against the Vikings on Nov. 22, if veteran wide receiver Mike Evans (Achilles) is cleared to return for that contest.

With Deebo Samuel still working his way back to 100 percent off his hamstring injury, Keenan Allen being eased in after his acquisition from the Colts and Mike Evans (Achilles) remaining inactive, Watkins' 44 snaps led San Francisco's wideouts. However, his three targets were a distant fourth on the team and represented just a 10.7 percent share. Allen will likely play more moving forward, and Evans is expected back in the bear future. Watkins doesn't have much fantasy appeal as an ancillary option.

Pineiro made his only field-goal try from 28 yards in the second quarter. The kicker has now gone eight straight games without making multiple field goals, and his next chance to snap that streak will come in Week 11 against the Vikings' impressive defense.

Allen looked rejuvenated in his 49ers debut after coming over from the Colts at the deadline, finishing third in receptions and receiving yards and second in targets for his new squad in the wild win. Allen and Brock Purdy seemed to have instant chemistry despite having practiced on only three occasions coming into the contest, and the veteran receiver's production should have a good chance of spiking further down the stretch of the regular season.

Kittle put together a very solid fantasy performance that was easily lost in the shuffle of multiple spectacular efforts by players on either side. However, the veteran tight end did pace the 49ers in receptions and targets while finishing second in receiving yards, and he's now recorded at least 70 yards on five occasions this season. Kittle is up to a 44-557-5 line on 62 targets through nine games as a Week 11 home showdown against the Vikings next Sunday night approaches.

Samuel made his return from a three-game absence due to a hamstring injury, and the versatile veteran was put right to work as the de facto No. 1 receiver with Mike Evans (Achilles) still sidelined. Samuel came just a yard short of tying his single-game career high in rushing yards, and his receiving and rushing touchdowns came from 11 and 70 yards out, respectively. Samuel has five total touchdowns through six games heading into a Week 11 home matchup against a tough Vikings defense next Sunday night.

Coach Mike MacDonald dialed up the blitz against rookie first-overall pick Fernando Mendoza in his first career start. Two of Witherspoon's four tackles in the Seahawks' win came behind the line of scrimmage off cornerback blitzes against Mendoza. Witherspoon also played all 59 of the team's defensive snaps in the one-score win.

Jones helped make first-overall pick Fernando Mendoza's NFL debut miserable. The inside linebacker helped the Seahawks' defense contain the young quarterback's scrambling ability while also limiting his mid-range opportunities from the pocket en route to yet another defensive win for the defending champs.
