Myers missed a 44-yard field-goal attempt with 7:05 remaining in the game that would have put the Seahawks up 14 points. The kicker is now 16-for-19 on field-goal attempts and 21-for-23 on PATs over 10 regular-season contests in 2026.

It was the third time this season that Kupp recorded only one catch, but the veteran wide receiver made his lone reception count when he found open space on a broken play to connect with Drew Lock for a TD late in the first quarter. It was the third touchdown catch of the season for Kupp, two of which have come over his last three outings. He'll enter the bye with a 23-272-3 line on 35 targets through 10 regular-season games, and the Seahawks' next matchup will take place in Week 12 on the road against the 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Horton failed to reel in a pass for the first time since Week 7, and his 10 offensive snaps ranked fourth at wide receiver for Seattle behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba (43), Cooper Kupp (35) and Rashid Shaheed (25). Horton will continue to be an unappealing fantasy option as long as he's buried below the other three wideouts on the depth chart.

Holani exited Sunday's Week 10 game against the Raiders after suffering a knee injury. The 26-year-old is not currently expected to be placed on injured reserve, but he will be reevaluated after Seattle's Week 11 bye. The three-year pro has had a larger role on special teams since Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price returned from injuries to helm Seattle's ground attack.

Darnold, who last played in Week 8, still is working his way through a pair of injuries, but barring any setbacks, he's trending toward a Week 12 return. Macdonald reiterated that Darnold will be the team's starter once healthy, even though backup Drew Lock has guided Seattle to a 4-0 record while coming on in relief or starting in place of an injured Darnold in the first two games of the season as well as the most recent two contests.

Barner has been held below 25 receiving yards in eight of 10 games this season and has more rushing touchdowns (two) than receiving scores (one) during the 2026 campaign. He's the definition of a low-floor, touchdown-or-bust fantasy option headed into the team's bye week.

After missing the previous two games with a knee injury, Shaheed returned against Las Vegas and maintained his role as the WR3 for Seattle. He played 25 of 57 offensive snaps and remained a non-factor in the box score. Shaheed has yet to hit 70 receiving yards in a game this season and has zero touchdowns as a pass catcher. He's off the fantasy radar.

Lock took advantage of having WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba at his disposal, targeting him 10 times, one of which resulted in a 71-yard TD connection. Moreover, Lock also hooked up with Cooper Kupp on a sliding 34-yard touchdown, marking his second multi-TD outing in four appearances (three starts) this season. There's an expectation that Seahawks No. 1 QB Sam Darnold (quadriceps) returns from a two-game absence after the team's Week 11 bye, but until he receives a clean bill of health, Lock has a chance to be under center on the road against the 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

This marks Price's fewest touches in a game since returning from IR in Week 8, and he actually was doubled up in the category by position mate Zach Charbonnet, who turned his 20 rushes into 94 yards. Having said that, Price salvaged his day with a 12-yard TD, the first of his career, on the ground in the third quarter. The breakdown of work between the two may signal what's to come in the Seahawks backfield after the team's Week 11 bye, with Price and company set to face off with the NFC West-leading 49ers on the road on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Charbonnet was eased in to the mix in Weeks 8 and 9, going from nine touches in the first contest to 17 in the latter. This time around, though, he doubled up fellow RB Jadarian Price in touches (10) and more than did so in terms from yards from scrimmage (44). It may signal that Charbonnet is the Seahawks' clear-cut No. 1 backfield option moving forward, but he won't have a chance to prove as much until after the team's Week 11 bye on Sunday, Nov. 29, at San Francisco.

Smith-Njigba's Week 10 performance was fueled by a 71-yard catch and run for a touchdown in the middle of the third quarter, but he still was able to put up 100 yards on his other seven receptions en route to a new season high in the category. As the Seahawks hit their Week 11 bye, he's reached the century mark in receiving eight times and resides on a 79-1,207-10 line on 109 targets through 10 contests. Smith-Njigba's next chance to continue aggravating opposing defenses arrives Sunday, Nov. 29, at San Francisco.

Reed limped off the field during the first half and was subsequently deemed doubtful to return. Brandon Pili should get a lot more defensive snaps in the likely scenario that Reed is unable to re-enter Sunday's contest.

Lucas exited the first quarter of Sunday's game with an ankle injury. The right tackle appears to have sustained a significant injury and likely will not return to the contest. Josh Jones should finish the game at right tackle for the Seahawks.

Since Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price returned to the lineup in Week 8 against the Bears, Wilson was contained to special teams in that contest and then was active but didn't log a snap last Sunday versus the Cardinals. Now, Wilson will yield all the RB reps to Charbonnet, Price and George Holani in Week 10.

Pili missed the Seahawks' last two games while nursing a back injury, but he's been cleared to play in Week 10 after logging a full practice session Friday. His return gives the Seahawks more depth on the interior defensive line behind Byron Murphy.

Nwosu has missed the Seahawks' last two games while tending to an ankle injury, but he's been cleared to play Sunday after ending Week 10 prep with a full practice Friday. His return means less defensive snaps will be available for Derick Hall, Dante Fowler and Connor O'Toole.

Hall was limited in each of the first two practices of Week 10 prep before sitting out Friday's session. However, his reduced practice reps appear to have been planned by the Seahawks to manage his back injury, and the fourth-year pro has been given the green light to play in Sunday's contest. Hall has 24 tackles (14 solo), including 3.0 sacks, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery through nine regular-season games.

Mayfield came out of the Buccaneers' Week 10 bye with a foot injury, which kept him out of drills Wednesday. After resuming on-field work Thursday, he relayed to Scott Smith of the team's official site that he felt good and was "limited," the latter of which has been confirmed. Per NFL reporter Andrew Siciliano, Mayfield also said, "If I feel like [Jalon Daniels] gives us a better chance to win, I have no shame in admitting that." As a result, it appears as if both Mayfield and Daniels have a chance to be under center for Tampa Bay on Sunday at Detroit.

Hayes started the regular season on injured reserve after undergoing surgery on his knee. He was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, but Hayes would need to be activated from IR in order to be available for Sunday's game against the Lions.

After exiting the Buccaneers' Nov. 8 loss to the Bears with the ankle injury, Winfield didn't show enough improvement during the team's Week 10 bye to get back on the field for the start of Week 11 prep. The 28-year-old safety will have two more opportunities to log practice reps before the Buccaneers decide on his status for Sunday's game against the Lions.
questionable

While the Buccaneers aren't ruling Mayfield out from playing Sunday in Detroit, the fact that he'll be a spectator in practice coming out of a Week 10 bye suggests that Daniels has the early edge on the Week 11 start. Per Auman, Mayfield appeared to be walking normally off to the side during Wednesday's practice, which could indicate that he'll attempt to test out his strained foot during Thursday's session. The Buccaneers should have some clarity by Friday whether Daniels or Mayfield will draw the start Sunday, with Mayfield's activity (or lack thereof) over the next two days likely to be the determining factor.

Stick has been a member of the Buccaneers' practice squad all season, with Tampa Bay having previously elevated him from Weeks 4 through 6 to back up Jalon Daniels while he filled in as the starter in place of Baker Mayfield, who was out due to a dislocated thumb. Mayfield has since moved past that injury, but he's currently nursing a sprained foot coming out of the Buccaneers' Week 9 loss to the Bears. Tampa Bay's decision to sign Stick implies some concern about Mayfield's status heading into Sunday's game against the Lions, potentially setting the stage for Stick to back up Daniels for the fourth time this season.

As a team, the Bucs picked off Caleb Williams four times Sunday night, but it still wasn't enough to propel Tampa Bay to a win. Smith now has two picks over his last three games and is up to 50 tackles (26 solo), three pass breakups and a forced fumble across nine starts this season. He has a chance to best last season's career-high 100 tackles in 2026.

The cornerback has been on an absolute heater in the interceptions department, as he's now recorded at least one pick in three straight games. After picking off Bryce Young and Michael Penix in back-to-back games, McCollum got Caleb Williams twice in Week 9. The four interceptions are a new career high for the fifth-year defensive back, who is now up to 35 tackles (28 solo), 11 pass breakups and a fumble recovery across nine games this season.

The Buccaneers picked off Caleb Williams four times, which included Anzalone's pick late in the third quarter that set up Tampa Bay in Chicago territory. Anzalone recorded four interceptions over his first nine NFL seasons, but he's already up to four picks in 2026, three of which have come over his last two outings. He enters the Week 10 bye with 44 tackles (19 solo), including 1.0 sacks, through nine regular-season games.

Trotter led the Buccaneers in tackles in Week 9, when he played 59 of 61 defensive snaps (96.7 percent). The rookie second-rounder has logged at least six stops in each of the first eight games of the regular season, and he enters the Week 10 bye with 76 tackles (37 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and three pass defenses (including a pick-six).

Johnson, a reserve wide receiver, has been used almost exclusively on special teams through his two-plus seasons in Tampa Bay. He's logged just 15 total snaps on offense through nine games in 2026, recording a three-yard reception on two targets. Johnson leads the Buccaneers with 14 kickoff returns for 389 yards, but he didn't see any runback opportunities in Week 9 while Sean Tucker handled those duties.

For a third consecutive game, the rookie third-rounder didn't record a catch while seeing only one target. Of more concern was the fact that Hurst was on the field for only one offensive snap in Week 9 after logging at least 25 offensive snaps in each of the first eight games of the regular season. That lack of offensive playing time coincided with the return of Emeka Egbuka, although Hurst also saw less snaps than Chris Godwin (62), Tez Johnson (52) and even David Sills (six), although Sills was cut by the Buccaneers on Tuesday. With the Buccaneers on a bye for Week 10, Hurst will look for better results in Week 11 against the Lions on Sunday, Nov. 22.

Johnson accounted for the Bucs' longest play of the game, producing a 58-yard catch-and-run to lead the team in receiving yards. Johnson has been working as the Bucs' WR3 behind Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin, with rookie Ted Hurst mixing in for sub-package snaps. Johnson isn't a particularly exciting fantasy bet.

It was the second straight week in which Tucker went without an offensive snap. That's happened despite Tampa Bay going to the ground plenty during that span. Perhaps not coincidentally, Tucker has begun working as a kick returner during the two-game stretch. It appears he's not going to get many opportunities on offense as long as Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell are healthy.

McLaughlin had a solid outing despite the loss, although all three of his field goals came from within 35 yards. Across his first nine outings of the season, the 30-year-old has yet to miss a kick, converting on all 22 field-goal attempts and all 18 extra-point tries.

The tight end saw a team-high eight targets, drawing a 26.7 percent target share from Baker Mayfield. It still didn't translate into much in the box score, as Otton remains without a touchdown through nine games. He's turned 38 targets into 23 catches for 211 yards this season and is a low-floor fantasy option most weeks.

Though he hasn't shown any signs of wearing down while he's averaged a healthy 4.9 yards per tote through the Buccaneers' first nine games, Irving has already amassed 167 carries -- fourth-most in the NFL -- and would be on pace for a career-high 315 over the course of a 17-game schedule. Given the success they've found on the ground in recent weeks, the Buccaneers could continue to embrace a run-first attack, but expect Irving to cede a bit more work to backups Kenny Gainwell and Sean Tucker as Tampa Bay aims to keep their top back healthy for the long haul.

While Bowles indicated that linebacker Yaya Diaby (knee) has decent odds of playing in the Buccaneers' next game Nov. 22 versus the Lions, the coach was less optimistic about McMillan's chances of being ready to play in Week 11. The Buccaneers have yet to open McMillan's 21-day practice window, after he was placed on injured reserve Sept. 30 due to a PCL sprain in his left knee, which was an aggravation of a previous injury. Bowles noted that McMillan underwent a medical procedure on the knee shortly after landing on IR and is still dealing with some discomfort.

Godwin has now gone back-to-back weeks without reeling in at least three passes after having done so in each of Tampa Bay's first seven contests this year. The wide receiver has yet to exceed 50 receiving yards or reach the end zone over nine games so far during the 2026 campaign, and he will remain an unappealing fantasy option when the Buccaneers return to action in Week 11 against the Lions.

Most of Gainwell's 76 scrimmage yards came on a 44-yard catch. He has 304 scrimmage yards over the past three games after recording just 122 scrimmage yards across his first six outings for the Buccaneers. Bucky Irving rushed for two touchdowns Sunday and remains the top option in Tampa Bay's backfield, but Gainwell has started to make the most of his change-of-pace role in the Buccaneers' run-heavy offense. Gainwell will try to pick up where he left off in Week 11 against the Lions after a Week 10 bye.

Egbuka returned from a two-game absence during which he was in concussion protocol in addition to dealing with a foot injury. He tied for second on the team in targets behind Cade Otton's eight and finished third in receiving yards behind Tez Johnson (76) and Kenny Gainwell (60), as Baker Mayfield spread the ball around to complement Bucky Irving's two-touchdown effort on the ground. Egbuka hasn't exceeded 63 yards in seven appearances this season heading into Tampa Bay's Week 10 bye.

Franklin-Myers appeared on the Titans' injury report with a back issue Wednesday, but it doesn't seem like it was anything too severe. He should again play a prominent role on Tennessee's defensive line in a Week 11 tilt against the Cowboys.
The running back returned to action last Sunday against the Jaguars and logged 16 snaps behind Tony Pollard's 41. Spears is only playable in Week 11 against Dallas as a desperation fantasy option.

Tate appears to be tracking toward a Week 11 return against Dallas after he's missed the last two games against Cincinnati and Jacksonville. The Titans could definitely use the rookie wideout after Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) was placed on season-ending injured reserve earlier this week. Tate's return would likely push Chimere Dike back into WR4 duties, with Xavier Restrepo the more sensible slot replacement for Robinson.
questionable

Gray was cleared to return from a one-game absence due to a concussion. The third-year linebacker led the Titans in both total and solo tackles, and he also picked off a pass from Trevor Lawrence intended for Jakobi Meyers midway through the first quarter, although Tennessee's offense was not able to convert that takeaway into points. Gray is up to 46 tackles (26 solo), including 0.5 sacks, and two pass defenses (one interception) through eight regular-season games.

Barton did not practice at all during the week leading up to Sunday's game versus the Jaguars, and he ended up missing that contest due to a concussion. He seems to be in a better position as the Titans begin preparing for their Week 11 game at Dallas, but he'll still need to clear league concussion protocol before he'll be allowed to return to game action.

The rookie second-rounder was unable to play in the Titans' 40-23 loss to the Jaguars in Week 10 due to a neck injury. Hill's return to practice Wednesday indicates that he is progressing in his recovery, and a full session over the next two days would put him on track to play against the Cowboys on Sunday.

Adams entered the league's concussion protocol during the Titans' 40-23 loss to the Jaguars in Week 10. Even if he returns to practice over the next two days, Adams would need to pass an evaluation by an independent neurologist in order to clear concussion protocol and be available for Sunday's road game against the Cowboys. Isaiah Oliver would likely start alongside Kevin Winston at safety if Adams is not cleared to play in Week 11.

Carmona returned to practice Wednesday as a limited participant in what was his first workout with the team since sustaining an ankle sprain in the Titans' Sept. 27 loss to the Giants. The Titans will have a 21-day window to evaluate him in practice, but once Carmona is deemed ready to return from IR, he could step into a starting role at either left or right guard.

Meanwhile Carnell Tate (shoulder) is slated to practice this week, and his potential return to action this weekend against Dallas figures to impact the playing time of Elic Ayomanor and Chimere Dike. Robinson's looming absence will free up snaps/targets in the slot, with Saleh noting Wednesday that he's looking forward to seeing what rookie slot option Xavier Restrepo can do with added opportunities going forward.

The fifth-year running back has suited up for all nine of the Titans' games this season, but he's been deployed almost exclusively on special teams as a member of the team's kick coverage and return units. He's played just two offensive snaps on the campaign and hasn't logged any carries or targets.

A 2025 undrafted free agent who played alongside Cam Ward during their final collegiate seasons at Miami, Restrepo showed immediate chemistry with the Titans' second-year quarterback during a 40-23 loss to the Jaguars in Week 10. Restrepo went on to play 19 snaps following Robinson's exit late in the third quarter and notched three receptions for 31 yards on three targets over the game's final 10 minutes. While the Titans are expected to get rookie first-round pick Carnell Tate (shoulder) back for Sunday's game in Dallas, Restrepo's strong showing in relief of the injured Robinson last week should at least allow him to stick ahead of Calvin Ridley (four snaps in Week 10) as Tennessee's No. 4 wideout.

With Carnell Tate (shoulder) out again, Dike played 54 of 57 offensive snaps against Jacksonville, but his three targets were a distant fifth on the team and represented just an 8.1 percent target share. Outside of his 5-71-1 receiving outburst in Week 8 against Cincinnati, Dike has amassed eight catches for 69 scoreless yards. He's not a reliable fantasy option, though a Week 11 date with Dallas' secondary awaits should Tate remain sidelined.

The blocking specialist played 28 of 57 offensive snaps and was asked to block on 12 of those plays. His two-yard touchdown in the second quarter was Bellinger's first of the season. For the year, Bellinger has 11 grabs for 76 yards and the score on 18 targets across nine contests.

Slye connected on field goals from 53, 54 and 50 yards during Sunday's loss, and he's now up to four makes from 50-plus yards on the year. He also made his way onto the highlight reel with a big tackle on a kickoff that forced the ball out of Josh Cameron's arms, although the Jaguars were able to recover the fumble. Through nine regular-season games, Slye has gone 15-for-16 on field-goal attempts and has made all 14 of his extra-point tries. Week 11 against the Cowboys could be a high-scoring affair, seeing as Dallas and Tennessee rank 30th and 27th, respectively, in points allowed per game.

Even though Carnell Tate (shoulder) was sidelined for a second consecutive week, Ridley was barely involved in the Titans' offensive game plan. Ridley's four offensive snaps were by far a season low, and his role figures to shrink even more given that Tate is expected to return for Week 11 against the Cowboys on Nov. 22. Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) could be sidelined for that contest, although those offensive snaps likely will go to Elic Ayomanor, Chimere Dike and even practice-squad wideout Xavier Restrepo rather than Ridley.

After a career day last time out in Week 8 against the Bengals, Helm's box score looked more familiar against Jacksonville's stout defense. He's been held below 30 yards in eight of nine games this season and has yet to catch a touchdown. Helm is a member of the large bucket of low-floor TE2 options in fantasy.

While he wasn't particularly efficient with the volume, Ayomanor led the Titans in targets and receiving yards on the afternoon, , and the receptions and yardage were both career highs, with Carnell Tate (shoulder) sidelined and Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) exiting the contest early. If they both remain on the shelf in Week 11 against the Cowboys, Ayomanor figures to handle an increased role once again. The second-year WR sports an 18-290-1 line on 36 targets through nine games on the year.

The veteran RB fell one yard short of reaching 100 scrimmage yards for a third straight game, and Pollard gave the Titans a brief glimmer of hope in the fourth quarter when he took a checkdown from Cam Ward 32 yards to the house, making the score 30-23. Pollard led the Titans in receptions as he produced season-best numbers through the air, and he could retain elevated usage as a pass catcher if top WRs Carnell Tate (shoulder) and Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) miss additional time. Pollard lines up for a potential revenge game in Week 11 against the Cowboys.

The second-year QB kept his team in the game for three quarters, and Ward connected with Tony Pollard for a 32-yard catch-and-run TD on a checkdown in the fourth quarter that brought the Titans to within one score, only for the Jags to pull away late. Ward's production is slowly creeping up, and he's thrown for 535 yards over the last two games with a 4:1 TD:INT, 68.4 percent completion rate and 6.8 YPA, numbers which represent a big step up from the beginning of the season. He'll look to keep making progress in his development in Week 11 against a vulnerable Cowboys defense.

Oliver had been elevated from the practice squad twice this season and logged seven tackles (three solo) and a defensed pass over 36 defensive snaps and 29 special-teams snaps. He'll now presumably work in a rotational role at safety on game days.

Coach Dan Quinn said Patrick has cleared the protocol, according to Nicki Jhabvala of The Athletic, so he should be ready to roll Monday night against the Bengals. He started all six games from Weeks 3 through 9 before being injured Nov. 8 against the Rams.

Martin played only 34 of the Commanders' 65 defensive snaps in Week 10 against the Giants, and a shoulder injury might help to explain why. Unless he's able to upgrade to full participation at practice Friday or Saturday, it seems like he's on track to carry an injury designation when Washington releases its final injury report of the week ahead of Monday night's matchup against the Bengals.

Yankoff sat out the Commanders' contest against the Giants in Week 10 because of a knee injury, but it now looks like he's put it behind him. He figures to resume a depth role at tight end in Week 11 against the Bengals.

The Commanders designated Croskey-Merritt for return from injured reserve Tuesday, and in the team's first official practice of Week 11 prep, he was uninhibited. Assuming he's able to maintain that activity level Friday and Saturday, he's a good bet to miss the minimum four games on IR due to the groin injury that bothered him multiple weeks through the first five contests of the campaign.

Though he's been active for five straight games while the Commanders' receiving depth has taken hits due to season-ending injuries to Terry McLaurin (knee) and Jaylin Lane (ankle), McCaffrey has yet to carve out much of a role on offense. He took the field for a season-high 14 of the Commanders' 69 offensive plays in Week 10 but went without a target. McCaffrey is likely to continue to provide his greatest impact on special teams, where he appears to have settled in as the Commanders' top return man on both kickoffs and punts.

Tunsil opened the season on injured reserve after undergoing surgery in August to repair a torn triceps. Though the left tackle isn't yet far enough along in the recovery process for the Commanders to know whether he has a legitimate shot at playing at some point this season, the team hopes to get clarity on that front in the weeks to come.

Reaves finished Thursday's game second on the Commanders in tackles behind rookie first-round linebacker Sonny Styles (13), and the former jumped on a loose ball caused by Frankie Luvu in the third quarter that stopped the Giants' red zone drive. Reaves has logged at least five stops in each of the first nine games of the regular season, and the veteran safety is up to 62 tackles (35 solo), four pass defenses and one fumble recovery on the year.

Cross was one of three Commanders players who played all 65 defensive snaps during Thursday's win. He's posted at least six stops in each of his last three outings, and over that span, he has accumulated 23 tackles (12 solo), three pass defenses (including one interception) and one fumble recovery.

Luvu stopped the Giants' red zone drive in the third quarter after punching the ball out of the hands of Malik Nabers, and Jeremy Reaves jumped on the loose ball to secure the takeaway for the Commanders. Luvu has played every single snap in each of his last three games, and he has accumulated 51 tackles (21 solo), including 1.0 sacks, one pass defense, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery over his last six outings.

Styles once again led the Commanders in stops while playing every single defensive snap. He has logged exactly 13 tackles in four of his last five games and is up to 80 tackles (37 solo), including 1.0 sacks, four pass defenses (including one interception) and one forced fumble through nine regular-season games. Styles' 80 combined tackles are third-most among rookies behind Anthony Hill (neck) (82) and Arvell Reese (81).

Stevens began the scoring in the contest with a 46-yard field goal early in the second period. That ended up being his only FG try of the game, but he made all three of his PATs. Stevens continued what has been a mostly fine rookie campaign -- he's made 17 of 20 field-goal attempts, with all three of his misses coming from 50-plus yards. However, he's just 15-for-18 on point-after tries.

Sinnott gave the Commanders a lead just before halftime when he reeled in a one-yard touchdown from Jayden Daniels. It was his first TD of the season and the third of his career. Sinnott's four grabs came out of nowhere, as he'd logged just one catch on two targets through his first eight games of the season. He also ranked third among Washington tight ends Thursday with 24 offensive snaps -- behind Chig Okonkwo (41) and John Bates (28) -- so fantasy managers probably don't need to go rushing to the waiver wire to pick him up. With that said, Sinnott may have earned himself more opportunities with Thursday's effort.

Burks missed Week 9 due to a foot injury but was able to limit his absence to one game. The veteran wideout logged a 60 percent offensive snap share, third among Washington wideouts behind Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams. Burks has a chance to take on a larger role in the Commanders' passing game with Terry McLaurin (knee) lost for the season, though Diggs and Williams may be better bets for weekly production given their higher spots in the pecking order.

Williams was a distant second to Stefon Diggs in receiving yards for the Commanders on the night, but like the latter, the former was on the receiving end of one of Jayden Daniels' three touchdown passes. Williams scored from 31 yards out just past the midway point of the third quarter, his first touchdown since way back in Week 1 against the Eagles. Williams hasn't been able to fully take advantage of the absence of Terry McLaurin (knee, IR) as of yet, but Thursday's score is certainly an encouraging sign heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Bengals on Monday night, Nov. 23.

As his final line indicates, Ekeler retained a solid level of involvement in the narrow win, logging a season-high 13 touches. He posted a new season high in receiving yards along the way, and the veteran back has proven to be a solid complement to Rachaad White while Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin, IR) has been sidelined. However, with the latter potentially set to return as soon as Week 11's home matchup against the Bengals, Ekeler could be headed to a reduced role.

White led the Commanders' ground attack once again, posting a team high in rushing yards and tying for the team lead in rush attempts with Jayden Daniels. The veteran back wasn't as involved as usual as a receiver, however, capping the overall quality of his fantasy performance. White also could see Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin, IR) make his return for a Week 11 home matchup against the Bengals on Monday night, Nov. 23, a development that would likely relegate the former to a complementary role he'd presumably share with Austin Ekeler.

Diggs paced the Commanders across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and his 32-yard catch-and-run touchdown grab over the middle with under a minute remaining sealed the win for Washington. Diggs tied a season high with his catch total while setting a new 2026 high-water mark in receiving yards and targets as well, and the veteran wideout should retain a prominent role throughout the second half of the season with Terry McLaurin (IR, knee) out the rest of the way in 2026. Diggs next takes aim at the Bengals' inconsistent secondary in a Week 11 home matchup on Monday night, Nov. 22.

It was a up-and-down night for Daniels in the narrow division win, as the third-year quarterback's pair of fourth-quarter interceptions threatened to derail Washington's fortunes. Daniels had the Commanders up by a 17-14 score just past the midway point of the third quarter after tossing one- and 31-yard touchdown passes to Ben Sinnott and Antonio Williams, respectively. However, Daniels subsequently squandered one scoring opportunity by throwing interceptions on back-to-back possessions in the fourth quarter, the first at the Giants' two-yard line. He ultimately made up for it with his game-winning 32-yard scoring strike to Stefon Diggs, marking the quarterback's first three-TD-pass tally of the season. Daniels is up to 1,499 passing yards and a 10:2 TD:INT alongside 280 rushing yards and another pair of scores heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Bengals on Monday night, Nov. 23.

Okonkwo exited in the second quarter due to a back injury, but he was back out there on the field after halftime and was the target on both of Jayden Daniels' two interceptions with less than six minutes remaining in the contest. Overall, Okonkwo's eight targets marked a season high, but he also mustered his fewest receiving yards since Week 4. He'll look to build upon his season-long line of 27-263-0 on 39 targets in the Commanders' next game Monday, Nov. 23 versus the Bengals.
